# Real-Time Breaking Analysis | IBM Think 2025: Arvind Krishna’s Enterprise AI Playbook

By [David Vellante](https://thecuberesearch.com/author/david-vellante/ "Posts by David Vellante")   | May 06, 2025

### Key Highlights

| Issue Enterprises Care About | IBM’s Prescribed Lever | Proof‑Points Cited by Krishna |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Productivity & Speed | **Watsonx Orchestrate** catalog of 150+ pre‑built agents; build‑your‑own in <5 min | “Client‑zero” savings: 125 K hrs/quarter in case summarization; 2× that in HR |
| Cost Efficiency | **Granite** small‑parameter models (3 B–20 B) tuned to verticals | 100–1,000× cheaper AI over time; lower inference cost than 300 B+ LLMs |
| Security & Sovereignty | Hybrid cloud + open‑source model zoo (Granite, Llama, Mistral) inside Watsonx | Focus on on‑prem and regulated‑industry use cases; data never leaves control plane |
| Integration Debt | **WebMethods Hybrid Integration** + HashiCorp stack | Single family for APIs, file transfers, workflows; accelerates ROI |
| Data Foundation | **Watsonx.data** lakehouse + forthcoming integration/intelligence modules | Lineage, ingestion fabric; Datastax vectors to power RAG workloads |

Source: Notes from Avind Krishna’s Think 2025 Keynote Commentary

---

### Hybrid Cloud + AI as Competitive Advantage

In our view, the twin pillars IBM touts of hybrid cloud and AI have moved from plumbing to profit driver. Krishna argued that technology is now a source of durable competitive advantage only when it both accelerates decision velocity and scales the business without proportional head‑count and footprint growth. At the same time this has to be accomplished with governance and trust in mind. We believe this framing resonates with CXOs who spent 2023–24 questioning GenAI ROI – i.e. they no longer need a science project—they need a P&L impact.

### Small Is the New Smart: IBM’s Granite Bet

IBM’s public dismissal of “massive, general‑purpose” models was perhaps the sharpest edge of the keynote. Citing internal testing, Krishna asserted that 3–20 billion‑parameter models tuned to narrow domains now meet or beat the accuracy of 300–500 billion‑parameter elephant models while slashing inference cost and hardware footprint. Our analysis of IBM benchmarking data (not publicly released, but directionally consistent with DeepSeek and Mistral disclosures) suggests a 7–10× cost delta per 1 K tokens in production. That gap widens further when workloads must run on prem or at the edge, where GPU power budgets are constrained.

> **Table 1 | Indicative Cost‑to‑Serve for Model Generations**
>
> | Model Class | Typical Params | Inference Cost Index\* | Tunability | Deployment Flexibility |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | Frontier LLM (GPT‑4 class) | 500 B+ | 100 | Low (RLHF) | Cloud only |
> | Mid‑size Foundation (Llama 3) | 70 B | 40 | Medium | Cloud / Large on‑prem |
> | **Granite / Domain‑Tuned** | **3–20 B** | **10** | **High (SFT + LoRA)** | **Cloud, on‑prem, edge** |
> | \*Index: GPT‑4 = 100 (higher = more expensive) |
>
> Source: IBM internal benchmarks, Meta technical docs, CoreWeave data

We believe this small‑model doctrine positions IBM as the anti‑hype vendor: instead of chasing ever‑larger parameter counts, the company is optimizing the *surface area* of AI—how many distinct business contexts it can penetrate.

IBM’s strategy aligns with data published by theCUBE [Research in 2023](https://thecuberesearch.com/breaking-analysis-the-gen-ai-power-law-how-data-diversity-will-influence-adoption/), focused on the Power Law of GenAI (shown below).

### From Experimentation to Integration: Watsonx Orchestrate

Krishna declared that “the era of AI experimentation is over.” His proof point is Watsonx Orchestrate, a catalog of 150 pre‑built agents covering HR, sales, procurement, IT ops, and customer service. IBM claims customers can assemble new agents in minutes; our conversations with early adopters suggest that figure is feasible after data connectors are wired in. What matters is not the GUI speed but the integration completeness—hence the simultaneous debut of WebMethods Hybrid Integration to knit APIs, file transfers, and workflows. We view the Orchestrate + WebMethods combo as IBM’s answer to Microsoft Copilot + Power Automate.

### Data Fabric: The Unsexy, But Important Layer

Every generative workflow ultimately chokes or thrives on data quality. Watsonx.data’s lakehouse, lineage, and ingestion pipelines aim to make that hygiene problem less painful, while the pending Datastax acquisition inserts vector search as a first‑class citizen, along with a world class real time data platform. In our opinion, the move is overdue—IBM’s own DB2 vector support lags category leaders—yet it closes a critical gap for retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG), a technique most enterprises are using keep proprietary data grounded.

### Ecosystem & Openness

Krishna hammered home that “the future of enterprise AI must be open.” That translates into three vectors of openness:

1. **Model Optionality:** Granite, Llama, Mistral MoE, and future OSS models are all accessible inside Watsonx.
2. **Hybrid Tooling:** Red Hat OpenShift and the HashiCorp stack provide cloud‑agnostic deployment and secrets management.
3. **Partner Solutions:** Oracle HR, Salesforce prospecting, Slack workflow agents, plus showcases with Ferrari F1, Sevilla FC, and telecommunications provider Lumen for edge AI.

We believe this approach is a direct counter to the vertically integrated stacks of AWS and Microsoft; IBM is betting that heterogeneity, not homogeneity, will characterize enterprise AI estates.

### Commercial Traction: Signals vs. Noise

IBM cites “300+ engagements” last quarter and a “book of AI business over $3 billion.” While the company offered limited segmentation, our research suggest that figure blends consulting, software licenses, and hardware pull‑through. The more instructive metric may be IBM’s own “dog‑fooding” – what IBM calls “client zero,” which has achieved $3 billion in cumulative cost takeout from automation, hundreds of thousands of internal labor hours reclaimed each quarter, and rapid reuse of those learnings in customer playbooks. In our view, that loop of internal proof → external offer is the fastest way IBM can scale credibility and differentiates IBM.

---

### Implications

* **For CIOs:** The Granite small‑model strategy, and more efficient models like DeepSeek, demonstrate the power of more efficient models and provide a lower‑risk on‑ramp to GenAI that aligns with sovereign‑data constraints—particularly attractive in EU and highly regulated US sectors.
* **For Nvidia & Frontier‑Model Vendors:** IBM’s rhetoric reinforces an emerging narrative that could create demand for more efficient models to lower the costs associated with ultra‑large GPU clusters.
* **For developers and ISVs:** IBM’s intent in our view is to offer WebMethods Hybrid Integration and open opportunities to refactor brittle pipelines into agent‑centric workflows.
* **For Competitors and Partners:** Microsoft’s Copilot ecosystem remains ahead in seat count, but IBM’s open, multi‑model posture may win accounts wary of vendor lock‑in. Partners like Salesforce, with Agentforce, and Oracle, are building out their own agent-based systems that will require connection points. IBM’s intent in our view is to be a sort of Switzerland of agent integration to drive customer value.

### IBM Z as an Enduring Platform

In our opinion, the single biggest misunderstanding about IBM’s mainframe franchise is that it’s a legacy drag. IBM’s [recent Z17 launch](https://thecuberesearch.com/ibm-z17-the-red-hat-enabled-ai-mainframe-revolutionizing-financial-services-beyond-a-blueprint-for-the-ultimate-ai-factory/) and Krishna’s Think 2025 remarks flipped that narrative Z17 is being positioned as an **AI‑first transaction engine** that complements, rather than competes with, Watsonx and Granite.

Perhaps more than seventy percent of the world’s structured financial data still lands on mainframes at some point in its lifecycle. By embedding Telum and Spire AI cores directly into Z17, IBM is eliminating the air gap between production data and AI models. The implication is that use cases like fraud‑scoring, credit‑risk models, or PCI‑bound personalization engines no longer need to shuttle data to an external GPU farm; or cobble together DIY on-prem solutions; rather they execute in the same cache‑coherent domain as the transaction itself.

This strategy also neutralizes a growing threat from hyperscaler AI databases. While AWS, Azure, and Google pitch real‑time fraud solutions that backhaul card swipes to the cloud, IBM is betting that large issuers will keep that logic inside the data center for latency and compliance reasons. If the 450 billion‑inference‑ops figure scales linearly across a multi‑frame sysplex as IBM claims, it places Z17 in a unique performance envelope that neither x86 nor Arm servers can hit without a costly GPU overlay.

IBM is hoping the Z17 transforms IBM Z from a legacy COBOL workhorse into an AI‑native enclave for mission‑critical, regulated workloads. It’s a big aspiration but For banks, insurers, and telcos already running Z, the upgrade math shifts from keep the lights on to value unlocks. For IBM, every Z17 refresh embeds Watsonx agents deeper into core transaction paths, tightening the flywheel between infrastructure revenue and AI software pull‑through.

---

### Bottom Line

Our view is that IBM has crystallized a coherent, differentiated AI thesis based on smaller, domain‑tuned models running on an open, hybrid‑cloud fabric. The goal is to unlock what it claims is the 99 percent of enterprise data still untouched by GenAI. If execution matches the marketing—particularly on integration speed and cost transparency—IBM will change the perception from perennial AI underdog to a primary or even default choice for risk‑averse enterprises seeking tangible ROI. The next two quarters of Watsonx bookings and Granite adoption will tell us whether the strategy is hitting escape velocity, merely clearing the launchpad or needs a reset.

# IBM: Navigating the Hybrid Cloud, AI, and Quantum Frontier (October 2025)

By: [PredictStreet](https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/news/provider/predictstreet)

October 04, 2025 at 10:07 AM EDT

ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness.

![Photo for article](https://news.predictstreet.ai/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/b3d16788-08a8-4e8d-8beb-5c179f36f3a7-1024x683.png)

IBM (International Business Machines Corporation), often referred to as "Big Blue," is a multinational technology and consulting company with a history spanning over a century. As of October 4, 2025, IBM remains a significant player in the IT industry, known for its extensive portfolio encompassing software, IT services, consulting, and hardware. The company operates in 175 countries, serving approximately 5,200 clients, including 95% of all Fortune 500 companies. Its core business activities include cloud computing, AI, data analytics, IT infrastructure, mobile, and cybersecurity, with a primary focus on enterprise customers.

**Why IBM is in Focus (October 2025)**

IBM is currently in focus due to its aggressive strategic shifts and significant advancements in key technological areas, particularly Artificial Intelligence (AI), Hybrid Cloud, and Quantum Computing. These initiatives are driving renewed investor interest and shaping the company's future trajectory.

1. **Artificial Intelligence (AI) Leadership:**

   * **Enterprise-Focused AI:** IBM is heavily investing in enterprise AI, positioning its `watsonx` platform as central to its strategy. The company emphasizes pragmatic AI applications, focusing on solutions that deliver tangible business value, such as cost reduction and efficiency gains for businesses rather than consumer-centric applications.
   * **Agentic AI and Small Language Models:** IBM is developing "agentic AI" systems that can reason, plan, and execute complex actions. It is also prioritizing small, efficient language models (like Granite 4.0) that offer competitive performance at lower costs and latency, crucial for agentic workflows and specialized enterprise tasks.
   * **Ecosystem Collaboration:** IBM is expanding its AI reach through strategic partnerships. A significant collaboration with AMD was announced in October 2025 to deliver advanced AI infrastructure, including a large cluster of AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs on IBM Cloud for training frontier multimodal foundation models. Additionally, IBM has partnered with AWS to accelerate secure cloud adoption and digital transformation in the Middle East, leveraging IBM Consulting's expertise and `watsonx` technologies. A collaboration with BharatGen in India aims to advance AI adoption using sovereign multimodal and Large Language Models tailored to India's linguistic and cultural landscape.
2. **Hybrid Cloud Dominance:**

   * **Strategic Core:** Hybrid cloud remains a fundamental pillar of IBM's strategy, especially after the acquisition of Red Hat. The company's roadmap for 2025 involves evolving hybrid cloud to support generative AI workloads on heterogeneous hardware, enabling cost efficiency, sustainability, and robust management across multiple clouds.
   * **Mainframe Reinvention:** IBM is reinventing its zSystems mainframes for the AI era, integrating AI inferencing capabilities and ensuring they remain vital for high-volume transaction processing within a hybrid cloud environment. This approach allows clients to integrate applications and data into hybrid cloud settings while leveraging the mainframe's strengths for AI-driven workloads.
   * **Data Fabric and Governance:** IBM's `watsonx.data` platform is evolving into a hybrid, open data lakehouse with data fabric capabilities, supporting unified access, governance, and AI readiness across hybrid and multi-cloud environments, which is critical for scaling AI initiatives.
3. **Quantum Computing Breakthroughs:**

   * **Ambitious Roadmap:** IBM has an ambitious roadmap in quantum computing, aiming to achieve a quantum computer with over 4,000 qubits by 2025 through a modular design. The company plans to demonstrate quantum advantage by 2026 and deliver a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer, named "Starling," by 2029, capable of running 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits.
   * **Real-World Application:** A significant recent development (September 2025) is HSBC's demonstration of the world's first quantum-enabled algorithmic trading, achieving a 34% improvement in bond trading predictions using IBM's quantum processors. This marks a pivotal moment, showing quantum computing transitioning from scientific curiosity to business reality and highlighting the potential for real-world revenue generation from IBM's quantum business within a few years.
   * **Quantum-Centric Supercomputing:** IBM's strategy includes "quantum-centric supercomputing," a hybrid approach that integrates quantum processing units (QPUs) with classical computing resources like CPUs and GPUs to tackle real-world problems.

**Current Relevance for a Stock Research Article (October 4, 2025)**

For a stock research article, IBM's current relevance stems from its ongoing transformation, strategic focus on high-growth areas, and recent financial performance, balanced against valuation and competitive pressures.

* **Financial Performance and Outlook:**

  + **Recent Momentum:** As of October 3, 2025, IBM's stock has shown strong momentum, rising 18.7% in the past month and 30.4% year-to-date. This positive trend is attributed to excitement around its AI and quantum computing developments.
  + **Q2 2025 Results:** IBM delivered robust Q2 2025 results with revenue up 8% year-over-year (5% adjusted for FX), strong margins, double-digit EPS growth, and record first-half free cash flow of $4.8 billion. The Software segment, particularly Red Hat (+14% growth), and Infrastructure (driven by the new IBM Z mainframe, +67% growth) were key performers.
  + **Upcoming Earnings:** IBM is estimated to report its Q3 2025 earnings on October 22, 2025, with Zacks Research forecasting an EPS of $2.43.
  + **Revenue Growth Expectation:** IBM expects currency-adjusted revenue growth of at least 5% in 2025, indicating an acceleration driven by its AI business.
* **Bullish Case:**

  + **Strategic Focus:** The rapid adoption of AI, hybrid cloud solutions, and digital modernization, especially in regulated industries, positions IBM for long-term growth and profitability.
  + **High-Margin Software:** The integration of acquisitions like Red Hat and HashiCorp (recently acquired), alongside innovations in quantum computing and automation, is expected to boost high-margin software revenue.
  + **Strong Cash Flow:** IBM's ability to generate significant free cash flow ($11.48 billion in the last twelve months, projected to rise to $14.67 billion in 2026) provides capital for investments and shareholder returns. The company expects to generate at least $13.5 billion in free cash flow this year.
* **Bearish Case / Risks:**

  + **Legacy Business Decline:** IBM still faces challenges from declining legacy revenues, which can offset growth in newer segments.
  + **Intense Competition:** The technology landscape is highly competitive, with strong rivals in AI and cloud computing.
  + **Valuation Concerns:** As of October 3, 2025, IBM's stock appears to be trading at a demanding valuation, with a forward P/E of 25x (compared to a historical average of 16x) and an EV/EBITDA of 17x. This suggests that the market has already priced in expectations of flawless execution of its AI and cloud strategy, leaving little margin for error.
  + **Moderate Growth:** While growing, IBM's projected revenue growth of 4% and EPS growth of 7% (forward) are lower than the sector average, indicating it's not yet a story of accelerated growth compared to some tech peers.
  + **Elevated Debt:** IBM holds a significant debt load of $58.40 billion as of March 2025, resulting in a net debt position.

In conclusion, IBM is undergoing a significant transformation, strategically pivoting towards AI, hybrid cloud, and quantum computing. While recent financial performance and strategic advancements in these high-growth areas present a compelling bullish case for investors, the current stock valuation implies high expectations for execution. Investors should closely monitor the company's Q3 2025 earnings report and continued progress in commercializing its advanced technologies, particularly in AI and quantum computing, to assess its long-term potential.

## 2. Historical Background

IBM, or International Business Machines Corporation, boasts a rich and transformative history spanning over a century, evolving from a manufacturer of diverse business machines into a global leader in information technology, driven by continuous innovation in computing, software, and services.

**Founding Story: From Tabulating Machines to International Business Machines**

IBM's origins trace back to the late 19th century, rooted in the need for efficient data processing. The earliest progenitor was Herman Hollerith, who began developing punch card-based data processing machines as early as 1884. His tabulating system was famously used by the U.S. Census Bureau for the 1890 census, significantly reducing the time and cost of data tabulation. Hollerith capitalized on this success by founding the Tabulating Machine Company in 1896.

The direct predecessor to IBM was formed on June 16, 1911, when financier Charles Ranlett Flint orchestrated the merger of four distinct companies into the **Computing-Tabulating-Recording Company (CTR)**. These companies included the Tabulating Machine Company, the International Time Recording Company (a manufacturer of time clocks), the Computing Scale Company of America (producing commercial scales), and the Bundy Manufacturing Company. CTR initially manufactured a broad range of products, from meat slicers and time recorders to tabulators and punched cards, with its headquarters in Endicott, New York, and approximately 1,300 employees.

A pivotal moment arrived in 1914 with the hiring of Thomas J. Watson Sr. as general manager. Watson, a dynamic salesman from National Cash Register, quickly ascended to president in 1915. He is credited with transforming CTR through a strong emphasis on sales, customer service, and an inspiring corporate culture, famously introducing the motto "THINK." Under his leadership, the company's focus sharpened on "business machines." In 1924, CTR was formally rebranded as **International Business Machines (IBM)**, reflecting Watson's global aspirations for the company.

**Early Milestones: Shaping the Information Age**

Under Watson's guidance, IBM achieved several early milestones that laid the groundwork for its future dominance:

* **Punched Card Innovations:** IBM continued to innovate in the punched card domain, introducing the 80-column punched card in 1928, which became a global standard for data input for decades. The company also developed electric accounting machines, first introduced in 1929.
* **Support for Major Initiatives:** By 1935, IBM played a crucial role in supporting the U.S. Social Security Act with essential record-keeping systems. During World War II, IBM significantly shifted its production to support the war effort, manufacturing various military ordnance items while limiting profits to a nominal one percent on war-related products.
* **Entry into Computing:** In 1945, IBM established the Watson Scientific Computing Laboratory, marking a significant step toward modern computing. The company unveiled its first large-scale digital calculating machine, the Selective Sequence Electronic Calculator (SSEC), in 1948. A major commercial breakthrough came in 1952 with the introduction of the IBM 701, its first mass-produced electronic computer for the commercial market, solidifying its presence in the electronics industry. This was followed by the IBM 704 in 1954, which was notable for being the first to feature indexing, floating-point arithmetic, and magnetic core memory.
* **Storage and Software Foundations:** IBM introduced the first commercial hard disk drive, the 350 RAMAC, in 1956. In 1957, IBM developed FORTRAN, one of the earliest and most enduring programming languages. The IBM 1401, launched in 1959, became the first computer system to sell over 10,000 units, indicating the growing demand for business computing.

**Key Transformations Over Time: Adapting to Evolving Technological Landscapes**

IBM's history is characterized by remarkable adaptability and strategic pivots in response to paradigm shifts in technology:

1. **Mainframe Dominance (1960s-1980s):**  
    The launch of the **IBM System/360 family of mainframe computers in 1964** represented a monumental transformation. This innovative system spanned a full range of commercial and scientific applications, allowing businesses to upgrade without rewriting applications, and quickly became the dominant computing platform globally. This era saw IBM evolve from a medium-sized maker of tabulating equipment into the world's largest computer company. In 1969, IBM "unbundled" its software and services from hardware sales, a significant shift in its business model. During this period, IBM also played a critical role in the U.S. space program, with its systems assisting the Apollo moon landing in 1969, and in daily commerce with the introduction of the Universal Product Code (UPC) barcode in 1973.
2. **The Personal Computer Era (1980s):**  
    In 1981, IBM entered the burgeoning microcomputer market with the **IBM Personal Computer (IBM 5150)**. This product had a profound influence on the personal computing market, legitimizing the PC as a serious business tool and spurring the development of the software industry. IBM's decision to adopt an open architecture, utilizing off-the-shelf components and third-party software (like Microsoft's DOS), fostered a massive ecosystem of compatible hardware and software. However, this openness also led to the rapid rise of "IBM-compatible" clones, which eventually eroded IBM's market share in the PC segment. By 2005, recognizing that the PC business had become a commodity, IBM divested its personal computer division to Lenovo.
3. **Shift to Services and Software (1990s-2000s):**  
    The late 1980s and early 1990s brought significant challenges, culminating in an $8 billion loss in 1993—the largest in American corporate history at the time. This crisis spurred another major transformation. Under CEO Lou Gerstner, who joined in 1993, IBM refocused on computer services, software, supercomputing, and scientific research. Key acquisitions, such as Lotus Software in 1995, bolstered its software offerings. The victory of IBM's Deep Blue chess program against world champion Garry Kasparov in 1997 showcased the company's leadership in artificial intelligence. This period saw a shift from a product-centric to a service-oriented business model, championed by CEO Samuel Palmisano from 2002.
4. **Hybrid Cloud and Artificial Intelligence (2010s-Present):**  
    The 2010s marked IBM's strategic pivot towards **cloud computing and artificial intelligence**. A landmark moment was the IBM Watson system winning the quiz show Jeopardy! in 2011, highlighting its cognitive computing capabilities. Under CEO Ginni Rometty (2012-2020), IBM intensified its strategic investments in hybrid cloud infrastructure and AI-powered enterprise solutions. A cornerstone of this strategy was the **$34 billion acquisition of Red Hat in 2019**, significantly enhancing IBM's open-source and hybrid cloud capabilities. Current CEO Arvind Krishna, appointed in 2020, has continued to steer IBM with a strong focus on hybrid cloud and AI, including the spin-off of its managed infrastructure services unit into a new public company, Kyndryl, to sharpen IBM's focus on its core growth areas. IBM is also actively leveraging its mainframe expertise for hybrid cloud optimization and AI innovation, developing platforms like Watsonx for generative AI and enterprise-level AI applications. This ongoing transformation aims to position IBM as a leader in digital transformation, integrating AI and cloud solutions for complex enterprise environments.

A pivotal achievement under his leadership was the landmark $34 billion acquisition of Red Hat, which significantly strengthened IBM's capabilities in open-source technologies and hybrid cloud. He has also prioritized the expansion into quantum computing and blockchain technology. **Strategy: Hybrid Cloud and AI Dominance**

IBM's current corporate strategy, particularly under Krishna, is sharply focused on leading the era of hybrid cloud and AI. The company's approach to AI is "full-stack, open, and enterprise-grade," integrating infrastructure software from Red Hat, foundation models from IBM Research, and customer enablement through IBM Consulting. IBM is betting on smaller, specialized AI models, deployed across hybrid cloud environments, and tightly integrated with its consulting services and data platforms, especially for regulated industries like financial services and healthcare.

### Innovation Pipelines and R&D

IBM's innovation pipeline and R&D efforts are heavily concentrated on advancing AI and quantum computing, supported by significant investment:

* **Generative AI & Agentic AI:** IBM is pushing for agentic AI systems that can reason, plan, and execute actions autonomously, transforming workflows and decision-making. The company is also developing both very large AI models (potentially exceeding 50 trillion parameters by 2025) and very small, efficient models for specialized tasks on edge devices. Context-aware AI is another focus, aiming for systems that interpret data within its situational context for improved customer service and internal operations.
* **Quantum Computing Roadmap:** IBM has an ambitious quantum computing roadmap extending to 2033.
  + **2025:** Plans to achieve a quantum computer with over 4,000 qubits by 2025 through modular design. The **Nighthawk** processor, coming in 2025, introduces a 120-qubit square lattice targeting 5,000 gate circuits, aiming for quantum advantage. The **Loon** processor is expected in 2025 to demonstrate technologies central to IBM's Quantum LDPC (QLDPC) error-correcting codes. The latest Kiskit runtime engine will also improve scalability of dynamic circuits in 2025, and error mitigation tools will be expanded.
  + **2026:** IBM believes the first demonstrations of quantum advantage on its quantum computers will occur by the end of 2026. The **Cucabura** in 2026 will be the first demonstration of a module in their fault-tolerant quantum computing architecture.
  + **2029:** IBM plans to deliver **Starling**, a large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer with 200 logical qubits capable of executing 100 million quantum gates. This represents a significant leap from current hardware.
  + **2033:** The **Blue Jay** system is envisioned to have 2,000 logical qubits, establishing the foundation for quantum-centric supercomputing.

This October 4, 2025 stock research article by PredictStreet analyzes IBM ("Big Blue"), a multinational technology and consulting company operating in 175 countries with ~5,200 clients including 95% of Fortune 500 companies.

KEY STRATEGIC FOCUS: IBM is pivoting around three pillars: (1) Enterprise AI via its watsonx platform, Granite small language models, and agentic AI systems, with partnerships announced October 2025 (AMD for MI300X GPU clusters on IBM Cloud, AWS for Middle East cloud adoption, and BharatGen in India); (2) Hybrid Cloud dominance anchored by the $34 billion Red Hat acquisition (2019), with renewed zSystems mainframes featuring AI inferencing; (3) Quantum Computing with a roadmap targeting 4,000+ qubits by 2025, quantum advantage by 2026, and "Starling" (fault-tolerant, 200 logical qubits) by 2029. In September 2025, HSBC demonstrated the first quantum-enabled algorithmic trading with a 34% improvement in bond trading predictions.

HISTORY: Founded from the 1911 merger creating CTR, rebranded IBM in 1924 under Thomas J. Watson Sr. Key milestones include the System/360 mainframes (1964), IBM PC (1981, divested to Lenovo in 2005), recovery under Lou Gerstner after an $8B loss in 1993, Deep Blue (1997), Watson Jeopardy win (2011), Red Hat acquisition (2019), and Kyndryl spin-off (2021).

BUSINESS MODEL: Revenue diversified across Software (largest source), Consulting, Infrastructure (including zSeries mainframes and Power systems), and Financing. Customer base includes 97% of banks worldwide and 47 of top 50 Fortune 500 companies using IBM Cloud. Full-year 2024 revenue was $62.8B; generative AI cumulative bookings exceeded $5B by Q4 2024. The $6.4 billion HashiCorp acquisition was finalized February 2025.

STOCK PERFORMANCE (as of Oct 3, 2025, closing at $288.37): Up ~43.44% over 1 year (from $201.04), 147.44% over 5 years (from $116.54, total return 208.11%), and 108.63% over 10 years (total return 213.77%). Stock hit all-time highs in February and June 2025 ($296.16).

FINANCIALS (Q2 2025, reported July 23, 2025): Revenue $17.0B (up 8% YoY, 5% constant currency); net income $2.194B (up 19.6%); operating EPS $2.80; Red Hat grew 14% with ARR of $22.7B; Infrastructure up 11% driven by new IBM Z (+67%); Consulting flat at $5.3B with gen AI book of business over $7.5B. Gross margin improved to 58.8% (GAAP). Record first-half FCF of $4.8B; full-year outlook raised to exceed $13.5B. Total debt $64.2B (core debt $52.4B); cash of $15.5B. Valuation: forward P/E ~25x (vs. 16x historical average), EV/EBITDA 17x, which is considered demanding. Q3 2025 earnings expected October 22, 2025 (Zacks forecast EPS $2.43).

Kavanaugh; Jay Gambetta became Director of IBM Research effective October 1, 2025. Board of 13 directors with Alex Gorsky as Lead Director. IBM was named in a UN expert report (June 2025) as central to Israel's surveillance apparatus.

# IBM’s Hybrid Cloud And AI Push Powers Major Q4 2025 Growth Across Software And Infrastructure

*‘As we laid out on our investor day in February 2025, we are executing on our strategy to advance IBM as a software-led hybrid cloud and AI platform company. We entered 2025 intently focused on investing in innovation and productivity initiatives to accelerate our shift towards durable, higher-growth end markets in software with expanding margins and strong free cash flow,’ says IBM chairman, president, and CEO Arvind Krishna.*

![](./media_11863e1b2b350bee5b88235190d984ae5cf2b4ec2.png?width=750&format=png&optimize=medium)

IBM has transformed itself into a software and AI company and in the process enjoyed a strong fiscal fourth quarter 2025.

Arvind Krishna, IBM chairman, president, and CEO, Wednesday told investors that the company’s 6 percent revenue growth for fiscal 2025 and 12 percent growth for the fourth fiscal quarter shows how well IBM has executed on its growth strategy.

“As we laid out on our investor day in February 2025, we are executing on our strategy to advance IBM as a software-led hybrid cloud and AI platform company,” Krishna said during his prepared remarks on the company’s fiscal fourth quarter 2025 conference call. “We entered 2025 intently focused on investing in innovation and productivity initiatives to accelerate our shift towards durable, higher-growth end markets in software with expanding margins and strong free cash flow.”

**[Related: [IBM: $9.5-Billion AI Book Of Business Drives Q3 Growth Across Software, Hardware And Consulting](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/ibm-9-5-billion-ai-book-of-business-drives-q3-growth-across-company-s-software-hardware-and-consulting-segments)]**

The numbers tell the story.

Software today represents about 45 percent of IBM’s business, up from about 25 percent in 2018, Krishna said.

“Software grew 9 percent, our highest annual growth rate in history, with three of our four software sub-segments delivering double-digit growth rates,” he said. “Innovation value can also be seen in our IBM z performance, up 48 percent this year, achieving the highest annual revenue for z in about 20 years. I am proud of our achievements in 2025 as we exceeded all of our target metrics for revenue growth, profitability and free cash flow that we laid out at our investor day.”

Customers appear to be investing in their IT infrastructures despite macroeconomic conditions, Krishna said.

“We continue to operate in a dynamic environment, but one where client demand remains resilient,” he said. “In the categories that matter most to IBM, enterprises are prioritizing technology investments that drive productivity, resilience, and flexibility, particularly in hybrid cloud, AI, and mission critical infrastructure. These technologies are no longer viewed as incremental tools, but as platforms that fundamentally change how businesses scale, compete and operate as clients modernize core systems, redesign workflows, and seek to extract more value from growing volumes of data.”

The 11 percent growth in fourth fiscal quarter software revenue exceeded IBM’s overall revenue growth of 9 percent, which was the company’s highest growth in over three years, Krishna said.

“Software growth [was] driven by the strength of our diversified portfolio,” he said. “Both data and automation are gaining strong momentum, with clients growing 19 percent and 14 percent respectively in the quarter, as AI adoption accelerates.”

Enterprises are increasingly focused keeping operations running smoothly in increasingly complex and hybrid environments fueled by a surge of new applications, Krishna said.

“Our end-to-end portfolio of leading automation and data solutions help clients manage and optimize operations, automate infrastructure and workflows, build resiliency, secure and govern data, and drive cost efficiency,” he said. “Consulting continued to grow, up 1 percent, reflecting increased demand for AI services as clients need help designing, deploying, and governing AI at scale.”

IBM also saw infrastructure growth in the quarter, with revenue up 17 percent thanks to robust sales of the company’s new Z17 mainframes, which is outpacing its Z16 performance, Krishna said.

“A key contributor to this momentum is the innovation value we are delivering with Z17, processing 50 percent more AI inferencing operations per day than Z16 and bringing real-time inferencing capabilities inside IBM z,” he said.

The breadth of IBM’s AI offerings is another key differentiator, with its innovative technology stack combined with consulting at scale leading to a cumulative GenAI book of business of over $12.5 billion, of which software is more than $2 billion and consulting is more than $10.5 billion, Krishna said.

“As we look at the evolution of AI, our opportunity is to make it easy for clients to build AI that is specific to their data, their processes, and their competitive needs, including the effective use of smaller, more efficient models where they make sense,” he said. “That is why IBM's approach spans consulting, [Watsonx](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/ibm-to-buy-datastax-expand-watsonx-ai-portfolio-s-data-management-capabilities), our [agentic platform Orchestrate](https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/ibm-to-expand-watson-orchestrate-automation-tool-access), and [Red Hat AI](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/red-hat-promises-ai-safety-boost-through-chatterbox-labs-acquisition),” he said. “Our announced [acquisition of Confluent](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/ibm-to-acquire-real-time-data-leader-confluent-in-blockbuster-11b-deal) is another pillar in this strategy, helping unify our hybrid cloud and automation solutions through a small data platform.”

IBM’s hybrid approach to models helps clients take advantage of the best option for each use case, including IBM's Granite models, third-party models, or open models from [Hugging Face](https://www.crn.com/news/cloud/2024/google-cloud-ceo-new-hugging-face-ai-partnership-makes-genai-more-impactful-for-developers), [Meta](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/scale-ai), and [Mistral](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2024/microsoft-backed-mistral-ai-startup-raises-640m-hits-6b-valuation), Krishna side. AI has also become a powerful productivity driver for IBM, he said.

“In 2023, we set out on a goal to achieve $2 billion of productivity savings exiting 2024, and today we are well ahead of that, exiting 2025 with $4.5 billion of annual run rate savings,” he said. “We have been accelerating our productivity initiatives to enable investment in innovation and highly strategic acquisitions like [HashiCorp](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/ibm-closes-6-4-billion-hashicorp-deal-after-extra-scrutiny-overseas) and Confluent, while continuing to deliver strong margin expansion and free cash flow growth

Accelerating organic innovation is a core focus for IBM, Krishna said. As an example, he cited Project Bob, the company’s next-generation AI-based software development system aimed at transforming developer productivity.

“Bob introduces intelligent orchestration between industry leading frontier models such as Anthropic Claude and Mistral, small language models including IBM Granite, and custom models, all optimized for cost and performance,” he said. “We have more than 20,000 IBMers that are using Project Bob reporting productivity gains, averaging 45 percent, a powerful client zero use case.”

IBM also unveiled new or deepened strategic partnerships through the year with AMD, Anthropic, AWS, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Oracle, Krishna said.

“Recently, we announced a partnership between Red Hat and Nvidia that aligns our hybrid AI solutions and Nvidia's AI stack,” he said. “This collaboration allows enterprises to deploy AI-accelerated applications across any environment from the data center to the public cloud using a unified, automated infrastructure. It represents a significant step forward in making high-performance AI more accessible and scalable for the hybrid enterprise. Innovation, combined with our strategic partnerships across consulting with key hyperscaler and ISP relationships and software with key data providers, drives a multiplier effect that fuels our flywheel for growth.”

IBM is also making steady progress in quantum computing, Krishna said. The past quarter saw IBM advance its development roadmap, improve error correction capabilities, and expanded ecosystem partnerships.

“Our collaboration with organizations such as Cisco and participation in government initiatives like the US Department of Energy's Genesis mission and DARPA’s Quantum benchmarking initiative reflect growing confidence in IBM's approach to building scalable, fault-tolerant quantum systems. Quantum advantage will require high performing hardware, and in December, we deployed our first 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk-based system for use by our clients.”

**IBM By The Numbers**

For its fourth fiscal quarter 2025, which ended December 31, IBM reported total revenue of $19.67 billion, up 12.8 percent from the $17.55 billion the company reported for its [fourth fiscal quarter 2024](https://www.crn.com/news/ai/2025/ibm-q4-2024-earnings-5-things-to-know).

This included software revenue of $9.03 billion, up 14.0 percent; consulting revenue of $5.35 billion, up 3.4 percent; infrastructure revenue of $5.13 billion, up 20.6 percent; and financing revenue of $179 million, up 5.3 percent.

Total revenue beat analyst expectations by $480 million, according to Seeking Alpha.

IBM also reported GAAP net income of $5.6 billion or $5.88 per share, up from last year’s $2.92 billion or $3.09 per share. On a non-GAAP basis, IBM reported net income of $4.52 per share, up from last year’s $3.92 per share.

Non-GAAP earnings beat analyst expectations by 23 cents per share, according to Seeking Alpha.

For all of fiscal 2025, IBM reported revenue of $67.54 billion, up from last year’s $62.75 billion.

This included software revenue of $29.96 billion, up 10.6 percent; consulting revenue of $21.16 billion, up 1.8 percent; infrastructure revenue of $15.72 billion, up 12.1 percent; and financing revenue of $737 million, up 3.3 percent.

IBM also reported full fiscal year GAAP net income of $10.59 billion or $11.17 per share, up significantly from last year’s $6.02 billion or $6.43 per share.

Looking ahead, IBM expects full fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of over 5 percent, the company said.

IBM stock soared in after-hours trading Wednesday, up nearly 8 percent.

[IBM Newsroom](index.php)



# All press releases

# IBM Unveils Next Chapter of watsonx with Open Source, Product & Ecosystem Innovations to Drive Enterprise AI at Scale

• Releases a family of IBM Granite models into open source, including its most capable and efficient Code LLMs that can out-perform larger code models on many industry benchmarks

• Jointly with Red Hat, launches InstructLab, a first-of-its-kind model alignment technique, to bring open-source community contributions directly into LLMs

• Unveils new vision and momentum for new data and automation capabilities; Accelerates generative AI infusion into IBM assistants, automation, infrastructure, resource management products and consulting services

• Strengthens collaborations with AWS, Adobe, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral AI, Palo Alto Networks, SAP, Salesforce, and SDAIA to expand capabilities and offer model choice, flexibility and governance through watsonx

May 21, 2024

![](/image/Think+23_Banner.jpg)

ARMONK, N.Y., May 21, 2024 – Today, at its annual THINK conference, IBM (NYSE: [IBM](http://www.ibm.com/investor)) announced several new updates to its [watsonx](https://www.ibm.com/watsonx) platform one year after its introduction, as well as upcoming data and automation capabilities designed to make [artificial intelligence (AI)](https://www.ibm.com/topics/artificial-intelligence) more open, cost effective, and flexible for businesses. During his opening keynote, CEO Arvind Krishna will share the company’s plans to invest in, build and contribute to the open-source AI community as a core part of IBM’s strategy.

“We firmly believe in bringing open innovation to AI. We want to use the power of open source to do with AI what was successfully done with Linux and OpenShift,” said Krishna. “Open means choice. Open means more eyes on the code, more minds on the problems, and more hands on the solutions. For any technology to gain velocity and become ubiquitous, you’ve got to balance three things: competition, innovation, and safety. Open source is a great way to achieve all three.”

**IBM released a family of Granite models into open source and launched InstructLab, a first-of-its-kind capability, in collaboration with Red Hat**

Furthering its commitment to the open-source AI ecosystem, IBM has now open-sourced a family of its most advanced and performant language and [code Granite models](https://research.ibm.com/blog/granite-code-models-open-source). By open sourcing these models, IBM is inviting clients, developers and global experts to build on these strengths and push the boundaries of what AI can achieve in enterprise environments.

Available today under Apache 2.0 licenses on Hugging Face and GitHub, the open-source Granite models stand out for their development process, quality, transparency and efficiency. The Granite code models range from 3B to 34B parameters and come in both base and instruction-following model variants, which are suitable for tasks such as complex application modernization, code generation, fixing bugs, explaining and documenting code, maintaining repositories and more. The code models, trained on 116 programming languages, consistently reach state-of-the-art performance among open-source code LLMs across various code-related tasks[[i]](#_edn1):

* Testing by IBM found that the Granite Code models overall show very strong performance across all model sizes and benchmarks, often outperforming other open-source code models that are twice as large compared to Granite.[[ii]](#_edn2)
* Testing by IBM on benchmarks including HumanEvalPack, HumanEvalPlus, and reasoning benchmark GSM8K showed Granite code models have strong performances on code synthesis, fixing, explanation, editing, and translation across most major programming languages, including Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++, and Rust.[[iii]](#_edn3)
* The 20B parameter Granite base code model was used to train IBM watsonx Code Assistant (WCA) for specialized domains. It also powers watsonx Code Assistant for Z — a product designed to help enterprises transform monolithic COBOL applications into services optimized for IBM Z.
* The 20B parameter Granite base code model was tuned to generate SQL from natural language questions for the purpose of transforming structured data and extracting insights from that data. IBM demonstrated leadership in natural language to SQL, an important industry use case, as benchmarked by BIRD's independent leaderboard, which ranks models according to Execution Accuracy (EX) and Valid Efficiency Score (VES).[[iv]](#_edn4)

IBM and Red Hat also recently launched [InstructLab](https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/ai/what-is-instructlab) — a revolutionary approach to advancing true open-source innovation around LLMs.

The InstructLab methodology allows for continuous development of base models through constant incremental contributions, much like software development has worked in open source for decades. With InstructLab, developers can build models specific to their business domains or industries with their own data, so that they can see the direct value of AI rather than just the model providers seeing the value. IBM plans to harness these open-source contributions to bring additional value to its clients through integrations with watsonx.ai and the new Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI (RHEL AI) solution.

RHEL AI comprises an enterprise-ready version of the InstructLab, IBM’s open-source Granite models, and the world’s leading enterprise Linux platform to simplify AI deployment across hybrid infrastructure environments. [*Read this blog to learn more about Instruct Lab and watsonx.ai.*](https://www.ibm.com/blog/announcement/democratizing-large-language-model-development-with-instructlab-support-in-watsonx-ai/)

IBM Consulting is also launching a practice to help clients leverage InstructLab with their own proprietary data to train purpose-specific AI models that can be scaled to better fit the cost and performance requirements of an enterprise’s business needs. [*Read this blog to learn more about how IBM Consulting is helping enterprises adopt AI.*](https://newsroom.ibm.com/Blog-IBM-Consulting-Expands-Capabilities-to-Help-Enterprises-Scale-AI)

**IBM unveils a new class of watsonx assistants**

This new wave of AI innovation has the potential to unlock an estimated $4 trillion in annual economic benefits across industries.[[v]](#_edn5) However, IBM’s annual Global AI Adoption Index recently found that while 42% of enterprise-scale companies (> 1,000 employees) surveyed have implemented AI in their business, another 40% of those companies that are exploring or experimenting with AI have yet to deploy their models. For the companies stuck in the sandbox, 2024 is the year of overcoming barriers to entry such as the skills gap, data complexity and – perhaps most importantly – trust.

To address these challenges, IBM is announcing several upcoming updates and enhancements to its family of watsonx assistants, along with an upcoming [capability in watsonx Orchestrate](http://www.ibm.com/blog/announcements/watsonx-orchestrate-ai-z-assistant) to help clients build their own AI Assistants across domains.

The new AI Assistants include watsonx Code Assistant for Enterprise Java Applications (planned availability in October 2024), watsonx Assistant for Z to transform how users interact with the system to quickly transfer knowledge and expertise (planned availability in June 2024), and an expansion of watsonx Code Assistant for Z Service with code explanation to help clients understand and document applications through natural language (planned availability in June 2024). *Read more on* [*watsonx Code Assistant for Enterprise Java Applications*](https://www.ibm.com/blog/announcement/watsonx-code-assistant-java/)*,* [*watsonx Assistant for Z,*](http://www.ibm.com/blog/announcements/watsonx-orchestrate-ai-z-assistant) *and* [*Watsonx Code Assistant for Z*](https://www.ibm.com/blog/announcement/ibm-watsonx-code-assistant-for-z-accelerate-the-application-lifecycle-with-generative-ai-and-automation/)*.*

IBM is expanding its NVIDIA GPU offerings to now offer NVIDIA L40S and NVIDIA L4 Tensor Core GPUs, as well as support for Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI (RHEL AI) and OpenShift AI to help enterprises and developers address the needs of AI and other mission-critical workloads. Additionally, to help clients accelerate time to value for AI, IBM is using deployable architectures for watsonx to enable quick AI deployment while empowering enterprises with security and compliance capabilities to help them protect their data and manage compliance controls. [*Read this blog to learn more about IBM Cloud capabilities*](https://newsroom.ibm.com/Blog-How-IBM-Cloud-is-Accelerating-Business-Outcomes-with-Gen-AI)*.*

Additionally, IBM has announced several new and upcoming generative AI powered data products and capabilities to augment how organizations observe, govern, and optimize their increasingly robust and complex data for AI workloads. Learn more about the upcoming IBM [Data Product Hub](http://www.ibm.com/blog/announcements/data-product-hub) (planned availability in June 2024), Data Gate for watsonx (planned availability in June 2024), and a host of the latest and planned updates on watsonx.data. [*Read this blog to learn more about these data capabilities.*](https://www.ibm.com/blog/announcement/delivering-superior-price-performance-and-enhanced-data-management-for-ai-with-ibm-watsonx-data/)

**IBM previews new vision and capabilities for AI-powered automation**

Hybrid cloud and AI are transforming how companies do business. The average enterprise today manages multiple cloud environments — public and private — and around 1,000 apps,[[vi]](#_edn6) each with multiple dependencies. They also deal with petabytes of data. With generative AI expected to drive up to 1 billion apps by 2028,[[vii]](#_edn7) automation is no longer an option – it is how businesses will save time, solve problems, and make decisions faster.

IBM is addressing these challenges by delivering a set of AI-powered automation capabilities that will allow CIOs to move from proactive management of their IT environments to AI-powered predictive automation. AI-powered automation will be an essential tool for driving the speed, performance, scalability, security, cost efficiency of an enterprise's infrastructure.

Today, IBM’s portfolio of automation, networking, data, application, and infrastructure management products help businesses manage their increasingly complex IT environments. For technology business management, [Apptio](https://www.apptio.com/blog/apptio-introduces-new-products-to-elevate-technology-value/) enables organizations to make informed, data-driven decisions about their investments by driving clarity on technology spend and how it drives business value — enabling organizations to quickly respond to changing market conditions. Clients can also combine Apptio with the power of [Instana](https://newsroom.ibm.com/Blog-Unlock-Operational-Excellence-with-IBM-Instanas-Intelligent-Remediation) for automated observability and [Turbonomic](https://www.ibm.com/blog/announcement/optimize-gpu-resources-turbonomic/) for performance optimization to help clients efficiently allocate resources and control IT spend through enhanced visibility and real-time insights, allowing them to focus more time on deploying and scaling AI to drive new innovative initiatives.

To complement these products, IBM [recently announced](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2024-04-24-IBM-to-Acquire-HashiCorp-Inc-Creating-a-Comprehensive-End-to-End-Hybrid-Cloud-Platform) its intent to acquire HashiCorp, which helps organizations automate multi-cloud and hybrid environments with Infrastructure Lifecycle Management and Security Lifecycle Management with products including Terraform, Vault and others. With HashiCorp, clients can easily move to and operate across multi-cloud and hybrid cloud environments.

Now, at THINK, IBM is continuing to advance its state-of-the-art in automation portfolio by previewing a new generative AI-powered tool called IBM Concert, which will be generally available in June 2024. IBM Concert will serve as the ‘nerve center’ of an enterprise’s technology and operations.

Powered by AI from watsonx, IBM Concert will provide generative AI-driven insights across clients’ portfolios of applications to identify, predict, and suggest fixes for problems. The new tool integrates into clients’ existing systems, using generative AI to connect with data from their cloud infrastructure, source repositories, CI/CD pipelines and other existing application management solutions to build out a detailed view of their connected applications.

By allowing clients to eliminate unnecessary tasks and accelerate others, Concert is designed to make teams more informed so they can be fast and responsive in addressing issues and solving problems before they happen. Concert will initially focus on helping application owners, SREs and IT leaders gain insights about, pre-empt and more quickly address issues around application risk and compliance management. [*Read this blog to learn more about IBM Concert.*](https://newsroom.ibm.com/Blog-Introducing-IBM-Concert-Control-your-operations-with-generative-AI-insights)

args.summary:
On May 21, 2024, at its annual THINK conference, IBM announced significant updates to its watsonx AI platform, one year after its introduction, alongside new data and automation capabilities designed to make AI more open, cost-effective, and flexible for enterprises.

**Open Source and Model Innovations:**
IBM open-sourced a family of Granite language and code models (available under Apache 2.0 licenses on Hugging Face and GitHub). These code models range from 3B to 34B parameters, offer both base and instruction-following variants, are trained on 116 programming languages, and consistently reach state-of-the-art performance among open-source code LLMs—often outperforming open-source code models twice their size. The 20B parameter Granite base code model powers watsonx Code Assistant (WCA) and was tuned for natural language to SQL generation, achieving top accuracy and efficiency scores on the BIRD leaderboard.

IBM and Red Hat launched InstructLab, a first-of-its-kind model alignment technique enabling continuous, incremental contributions to base models—similar to decades of open-source software development. This is integrated with watsonx.ai and the new Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI (RHEL AI) solution. IBM Consulting launched a practice to help clients use InstructLab with proprietary data.

**New watsonx Assistants and Tools:**
- watsonx Code Assistant for Enterprise Java Applications (planned October 2024)
- watsonx Assistant for Z (planned June 2024)
- Expansion of watsonx Code Assistant for Z Service with code explanation (planned June 2024)
- New generative AI data products: Data Product Hub (June 2024), Data Gate for watsonx (June 2024), and updates to watsonx.data
- Expanded NVIDIA GPU offerings (L40S and L4 Tensor Core GPUs) with RHEL AI and OpenShift AI support

**AI-Powered Automation:**
IBM previewed IBM Concert (general availability June 2024), a generative AI-powered "nerve center" tool providing insights across application portfolios to identify, predict, and suggest fixes. IBM also announced its intent to acquire HashiCorp and highlighted its Apptio, Instana, and Turbonomic products.

**Ecosystem Expansions:**
IBM strengthened collaborations with AWS (Amazon SageMaker + watsonx.governance integration), Adobe, Meta (Llama 3 on watsonx), Microsoft (watsonx on Azure), Mistral AI (strategic partnership), Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce (Granite on Einstein 1 platform), SAP (Granite accessible in SAP cloud solutions), and SDAIA (Arabic ALLaM model on watsonx).

**Key Context:**
IBM's Global AI Adoption Index found 42% of enterprise-scale companies have implemented AI, while another 40% exploring AI haven't yet deployed. CEO Arvind Krishna emphasized: "We firmly believe in bringing open innovation to AI. We want to use the power of open source to do with AI what was successfully done with Linux and OpenShift."

**Client Testimonials:** Featured deployments include Broadridge Financial, Casper Labs (Prove AI), UK Department for Work and Pensions, Dun & Bradstreet (Ask Procurement), Elevance Health (60% AI handling effectiveness in complex healthcare interactions), Medtronic, Sevilla FC (scouting insights from 400,000 player reports), Virgin Money (Redi virtual assistant), and Westfield Insurance (80% productivity improvement during an eight-week watsonx pilot).

## Executive Summary

International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE: IBM) is a 115-year-old technology company that has executed a multi-year pivot from legacy hardware and managed IT services toward a hybrid cloud and AI platform business -- successfully by most financial measures, though the pace of transformation continues to divide investors.

As of mid-2026, IBM operates four reportable segments: Software, Consulting, Infrastructure, and Financing.[11](#ref-11) Software -- home to Red Hat's OpenShift, IBM Cloud Paks, and the watsonx AI platform -- is now the largest revenue contributor and clearest growth engine. In Q1 2026, Software revenue grew 11% year-over-year to $7.05 billion, while the consolidated company posted $15.9 billion in revenue, topping the LSEG consensus estimate of $15.62 billion.[4](#ref-4) For full year 2025, IBM delivered $67.5 billion in revenue (up 7.6% vs. FY2024),[5](#ref-5) net income of $10.6 billion (up 76.7% year-over-year),[6](#ref-6) and record free cash flow of $14.7 billion.[6](#ref-6) IBM's generative AI book of business reached $12.5 billion in cumulative bookings by Q4 2025, validating early watsonx traction in regulated enterprise markets.[7](#ref-7)

The bull case rests on two compounding themes: whether IBM's watsonx AI platform can capture enough of the large-model deployment market in regulated industries -- banking, healthcare, government -- to sustain double-digit Software growth; and whether the z17 mainframe super-cycle and HashiCorp integration deliver lasting infrastructure stickiness. The bear case centers on decelerating topline growth (FY2026 guidance: above 5% constant currency,[4](#ref-4) versus 7.6% in FY2025), margin pressure in Consulting as AI automates billable work, and IBM's structural inability to compete head-on with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud for net-new public cloud workloads.[9](#ref-9)

04 · Business Model

## Business Model & Unit Economics

IBM generates revenue across four reportable segments -- Software, Consulting, Infrastructure, and Financing -- with a deliberate strategic tilt toward Software, which carries the highest margins and the clearest AI growth story.[11](#ref-11) IBM operates in more than 175 countries.[11](#ref-11)

### Software

Software is IBM's largest and fastest-growing segment, delivering hybrid cloud and AI platforms including Red Hat OpenShift, IBM Cloud Paks, watsonx, and (post-acquisition) HashiCorp Terraform and Vault. In Q1 2026, Software contributed $7.05 billion in revenue, up 11% year-over-year.[4](#ref-4) The Software business is predominantly subscription- and license-based, providing a high degree of revenue predictability and high gross margins. Red Hat's OpenShift is one of the most widely deployed enterprise Kubernetes platforms globally, creating deep switching costs once embedded across a client's development pipelines.

### Consulting

Consulting delivers business transformation, technology implementation, managed services, application modernization, and AI-powered solutions.[11](#ref-11) It is inherently labor-intensive, with margins that depend on utilization rates, talent costs, and the ability to up-sell higher-margin AI and automation tooling. This segment faces a structural tension: IBM's own AI products can reduce billable hours over time even as they attract new engagements in the near term. IBM Consulting is also one of the world's largest SAP implementation partners, with significant Salesforce and Workday practices.[11](#ref-11)

### Infrastructure

Infrastructure provides on-premises and cloud-based server and storage solutions, including the iconic IBM Z mainframe family and IBM Power servers.[11](#ref-11) The IBM Z mainframe is a near-monopoly for mission-critical workloads in global banking, insurance, and government. The z17 cycle drove Infrastructure revenue up 15% in Q1 2026,[4](#ref-4) with Z mainframe hardware specifically up 51% year-over-year -- a remarkable cycle performance. Mainframe cycles typically run 3-5 years, so the current z17 uplift creates both a near-term tailwind and a future deceleration headwind.

### Financing

IBM Financing facilitates clients' acquisition of hardware, software, and services through client and commercial financing arrangements.[11](#ref-11) This is a relatively small, low-growth segment that primarily serves as a sales-enablement tool for the other three segments.

### Moat and Growth Motion

IBM's competitive moat rests on three pillars: (1) deep enterprise trust built over 115 years, particularly in regulated industries with strict data sovereignty and compliance requirements; (2) the hybrid cloud platform stack assembled through Red Hat, HashiCorp, and IBM Cloud Paks, creating high switching costs once deployed; and (3) watsonx AI, which differentiates on governance, auditability, and on-premises deployment -- capabilities that hyperscalers do not prioritize for their standard AI services.[17](#ref-17) IBM's go-to-market motion uses Consulting to land and then expand Software relationships across the enterprise, creating a bundled land-and-expand cycle. The $12.5 billion generative AI book of business as of Q4 2025[7](#ref-7) provides early evidence that this motion is working, with analysts projecting IBM's AI revenue could reach $15 billion by 2027.[18](#ref-18)

09 · Competitive Landscape

## Competition

IBM competes across multiple technology markets simultaneously: hybrid cloud infrastructure, enterprise AI platforms, IT consulting, and mainframe hardware. In no single arena does IBM hold a dominant market-share position, but in each it occupies a credible, entrenched role -- particularly in regulated industries where governance and data sovereignty requirements favor IBM's on-premises and hybrid-first approach.

| Competitor | Status | Primary Arena | Differentiator vs. IBM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amazon Web Services (AWS) | Public (AMZN) | Cloud Infrastructure, AI Services | ~28% global cloud market share (Q1 2026); [9](#ref-9) broadest IaaS catalog; scale cost advantages |
| Microsoft Azure | Public (MSFT) | Cloud Infrastructure, Enterprise AI | ~21% cloud share; [9](#ref-9) deep Microsoft 365 enterprise integration; Azure OpenAI / Copilot across productivity suite |
| Google Cloud | Public (GOOGL) | Cloud Infrastructure, AI/ML | ~14% cloud share; [9](#ref-9) superior AI/ML capabilities (Gemini); leading data analytics (BigQuery) |
| Accenture | Public (ACN) | IT Consulting & Systems Integration | Larger consulting revenue base; broader vertical coverage; more technology-agnostic positioning |
| Capgemini | Public (CAP) | IT Consulting & Managed Services | Strong European presence; competitive on labor cost for infrastructure managed services |
| Oracle | Public (ORCL) | Enterprise Software, Cloud Database | Dominant in relational databases; Oracle Cloud growing rapidly; competes for ERP workloads |

Where IBM's competitive moat is most defensible: IBM Z mainframe. The zSeries runs an estimated majority of global banking transactions, with switching costs so high -- decades of COBOL workloads, certified operators, and compliance certifications -- that enterprises almost never migrate. The z17 cycle's 51% hardware revenue surge in Q1 2026[4](#ref-4) confirms this franchise remains remarkable durable.

In enterprise AI, IBM watsonx competes with Azure AI Foundry, Google Vertex AI, and AWS Bedrock as one of four dominant enterprise AI platforms in 2026.[17](#ref-17) IBM's governance and on-premises deployment differentiation is genuinely valued in regulated sectors, but hyperscalers are closing the compliance gap with their own enterprise AI governance tooling.

In IT consulting, IBM competes directly with Accenture and Capgemini, both of which are larger in aggregate consulting revenue. IBM's edge is its ability to cross-sell software and infrastructure alongside consulting engagements -- a bundled value proposition that pure-play consultancies cannot replicate. However, this advantage diminishes as clients increasingly separate technology selection from implementation services.

10 · Risks & Bear Thesis

## Risks & the Bear Case

Revenue Growth Deceleration

FY2026 guidance of "above 5%" constant-currency growth[4](#ref-4) is a step-down from FY2025's 7.6% reported growth.[5](#ref-5) Macro headwinds or AI bookings stagnation could push IBM toward or below this floor.

Hyperscaler Competitive Pressure

AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud together control 63%+ of cloud infrastructure.[9](#ref-9) Their scale, R&D budgets, and talent pools limit IBM's ability to capture net-new public cloud workloads.

AI Disruption of Consulting

IBM's own AI tools and the broader AI wave could structurally compress Consulting margins as clients automate tasks previously billed as professional-services engagements.[10](#ref-10)

Acquisition Debt Burden

The ~$34B Red Hat deal[13](#ref-13) and $6.4B HashiCorp acquisition[8](#ref-8) leave IBM with a substantial long-term debt load, limiting balance-sheet flexibility and further M&A capacity.

Mainframe Cycle Risk

The z17 mainframe cycle is currently boosting Infrastructure revenue (hardware +51% in Q1 2026).[4](#ref-4) Mainframe cycles run 3-5 years; the inevitable post-cycle deceleration can be sharp, impacting both revenue and investor sentiment.

HashiCorp Integration Risk

Integrating HashiCorp's open-source-origin products into IBM's enterprise sales motion carries risks of developer community friction, customer churn, and go-to-market complexity.[8](#ref-8)

Geopolitical & Macro Exposure

IBM operates in more than 175 countries.[11](#ref-11) Currency headwinds, trade restrictions, and geopolitical disruptions were cited explicitly by management as a reason for conservative 2026 guidance.[4](#ref-4)

Valuation vs. Growth Rate

Following the stock's ~21% three-month drawdown,[10](#ref-10) IBM trades at a valuation that still requires execution on AI and Software growth. If growth disappoints, the stock could re-rate toward a lower mature-tech multiple.

### Bear Thesis Deep Dive

The central bear argument on IBM is that its apparent financial renaissance may prove unsustainable at current growth rates. The FY2025 net income surge (+76.7% to $10.6 billion)[6](#ref-6) was partly aided by favorable year-over-year comparisons and one-time items; recurring earnings power is more modest. The FY2026 "above 5%" revenue guidance,[4](#ref-4) issued during acknowledged geopolitical uncertainty, signals that management is itself cautious about repeating FY2025's growth rate.

Trefis articulated a market-shock bear scenario in May 2026: if IBM's consulting revenue -- already facing AI automation disruption -- declines materially in a spending freeze or recession, and if the z17 mainframe cycle peaks sooner than expected, the stock could face a prolonged recovery period.[10](#ref-10) A Trefis analysis from June 22, 2026 posed the specific question of whether investors could be forced to "wait years for IBM stock to recover."[23](#ref-23) This scenario is amplified by the heavy acquisition debt, which limits IBM's ability to aggressively buy back stock or pursue transformative deals.

The bear case also questions watsonx's bookings-to-revenue conversion. IBM's $12.5 billion generative AI book of business[7](#ref-7) is a cumulative bookings figure, not annual recurring revenue. Enterprise AI bookings-to-revenue conversion can be slow and lumpy, particularly for large regulated-industry deployments. If watsonx fails to convert bookings into durable ARR at expected rates, the AI growth premium embedded in IBM's multiple is not justified.

args.summary:
This is a LinkedIn post by Armand Ruiz (an IBM influencer focused on building AI systems) showcasing examples of generative AI projects IBM has undertaken with clients and partners using IBM's watsonx platform. The post lists eight notable partnerships:

1. **Adobe** - Using watsonx.ai to help marketers analyze marketing data for better personalization.
2. **Samsung SDS** - Using watsonx.ai for product innovation to improve client experience.
3. **NASA** - Leveraging foundation models to detect natural hazards and track changes to vegetation and wildlife habitat.
4. **Dun & Bradstreet** - Using watsonx to bring new solutions to market trained on proprietary data, focused on improving procurement professional processes.
5. **Regions** - Monitoring private wealth retention models to detect drift in accuracy and data consistency and help mitigate attrition.
6. **Wimbledon** - Leveraged watsonx.ai foundation models to train their AI for an informative and engaging fan experience.
7. **Intel** - Achieving breakthrough performance by scaling AI workloads for all data with watsonx.data through Presto open-source.
8. **WIX** - Bringing customer care data to improve customer support.

The post references a link for more examples and details. The post received 401 reactions and 34 comments. Key commenters included Tore Notland (mentioning Mediehuset iTromsø involvement), Sebastian Paris (noting IBM's pioneering yet diminished AI lead), Ebrima Ceesay (asking about lessons learned), Shubham Verma (asking if projects are live or completed), Andre Felipe Lopes (highlighting Sicredi collaboration in Latin America), Edward Frank Morris and Dr. Saad Attieh (praising the NASA use case), and Mahesh Lambe (mentioning WatsonX implementation in the public sector).

# Accelerating software testing with automation and generative AI

ContextQA + IBM

![watsonx.ai digital rendering for leadspace](https://assets.ibm.com/is/image/ibm/ibm-watsonxai-a04?ts=1727894601139&dpr=off)

Software testing is the piece that is always lacking, and because of that, software releases are often delayed, and product quality is often compromised. ContextQA has developed an application that does not require any coding knowledge. Instead, it uses AI and automation to test web applications, APIs and mobile applications.

IBM is the biggest name in the market. It is a trustworthy brand, and all enterprise customers and Fortune 500 clients see IBM with the highest respect. Now our name is associated with IBM.

Deep Barot   CEO and Founder   ContextQA

5,000   test cases migrated and automated within minutes

Before generative AI, ContextQA started with automation. It met the IBM team at the South by Southwest (SXSW) event in Austin. The Build IBM Team provided the company with the opportunity to try out a new tool without needing more infrastructure. It was eye-opening because the IBM solution allowed ContextQA to use generative AI models and many out-of-the-box capabilities.

The company worked with the Build Partner team as a technical resource support for a month. The Build Partner team guided ContextQA on what options were available and how to use them for successful deployment. Without much training data, ContextQA wanted to migrate manual test cases and automate them across disparate organizational data. Using natural language processing (NLP) models that IBM provides, ContextQA was able to come up with a large amount of data and automate the manual steps. It was also able to solve for flakiness in software development.

ContextQA had tried OpenAI, but the company experienced several limitations. One of the main issues that ContextQA faced was the privacy and ethics around those models. It is crucial for enterprise customers to have secure, non-biased ethical models, and the [IBM® watsonx.ai™](https://www.ibm.com/products/watsonx-ai) studio solved that problem. ContextQA tried different solutions but couldn’t find the right answer, except with IBM.

With IBM AI technology, the company was able to identify what had changed in the software, provide relevant, accurate suggestions, and perform the correct tasks. So, flakiness in testing was gone using the IBM models.

“We used watsonx.ai studio to do the NLP-based migration of the manual test cases for larger enterprises with 5,000 test cases written in plain English in their Excel spreadsheet,” says Deep Barot, CEO and Founder of ContextQA. “We were able to migrate all those cases and automate them within a few minutes. This is the power of generative AI that IBM provides.”

IBM has a big ecosystem, its own DevOps tools and is backed by [IBM Consulting®](https://www.ibm.com/consulting) to develop cutting-edge technologies, which have proven advantageous for ContextQA in its ability to improve testing and reporting capabilities as well as open doors to many more enterprise customers.

About ContextQA

 

[ContextQA](https://contextqa.com/) (link resides outside of ibm.com) is a software product development company based in Austin, Texas. It has a software automation platform that automates application testing and quality assurance processes using single-click AI technology. ContextQA works with enterprises and startup clients throughout the software development process.

IBM watsonx.ai

Watsonx.ai is helping companies custom build AI solutions to suit their specific needs.
