# Capgemini profit falls 4.2% to $1.9bn despite revenue rise to $26.7bn

![](https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/453E2A1429BB65B639AE7E62CA5A9851DC6BF7EF53CE3E3AAC03C9723D1C9692/subgraphmysterio/resizefit_w960_h540;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fverdict_626%2Fb3f89d57d8593c27c309a32e298aa39f)

AI demand boosts Capgemini's 2025 revenue growth to 3.4% at constant rates. · Verdict · JeanLucIchard/Shutterstock.com.

BV Swagath

4 min read

* [CAPMF

  +0.27%](/quote/CAPMF/ "CAPMF")

Capgemini's net profit attributable to the group for the year 2025 experienced a decline of 4.2%, amounting to €1.6bn compared to €1.67bn in 2024.

Despite this decrease in net profit, the French IT major reported an increase in revenue, reaching €22.5bn, which represents a 1.7% rise compared to the previous year's revenue of €22bn. When adjusted for constant exchange rates, the revenue growth was 3.4%, surpassing earlier projections.

In terms of earnings per share (EPS), the basic EPS decreased by 3.7% to €9.46, while the normalised EPS increased by 5.8% to €12.95.

The company's bookings for the year totalled €24.4bn ($28.96bn), reflecting a 3.9% increase at constant exchange rates, and the book-to-bill ratio stood at 1.08.

The operating margin was stable at 13.3% of revenues, equating to €2.98bn. In terms of cash flow, Capgemini generated an organic free cash flow of €1.95bn, which remained stable compared to the previous year

In the fourth quarter, Capgemini achieved a revenue growth of 10.6%, driven by strong demand for cloud, data, AI, and digital business process services. Generative and agentic AI made up more than 10% of Capgemini's bookings in Q4.

The Q4 revenue growth was further supported by the strategic acquisition of WNS, which enhanced Capgemini's capabilities in delivering AI-powered intelligent operations.

The acquisition is expected to accelerate the end-to-end agentification of business processes, aligning with the company's strategic focus on AI integration.

Looking ahead to 2026, Capgemini aims to achieve revenue growth of 6.5% to 8.5% at constant exchange rates. The company also projects an operating margin between 13.6% and 13.8%, with plans to drive growth through AI-led transformation programmes and increased demand for sovereignty solutions.

Additionally, Capgemini is preparing for restructuring initiatives, with anticipated costs of approximately €700m over the next two years, aimed at aligning its workforce with its growth agenda.

Regionally, North America experienced a 7.3% increase in revenue, bolstered by WNS and strong performance in financial services. Meanwhile, the UK and Ireland saw a 10.5% growth, whereas France faced a 4.1% decline due to challenges in the manufacturing sector.

Other regions also contributed to the overall growth, with varying performances across different markets.

As of 31 December 2025, Capgemini's total headcount reached 423,400, marking an increase of 82,300 or 24% compared to the previous year. This rise includes an increase of 68,700 since the end of September 2025, largely due to the integration of WNS team members.

Capgemini CEO Aiman Ezzat said: "In a complex macroeconomic environment, we exceeded our revenue growth objective and met our margin and organic free cash flow targets, demonstrating the strength and clarity of our strategic direction.

"The improvement of our underlying growth dynamics throughout the year has been driven by a strong demand for cloud, data & AI and digital business process services, as well as a greater number of large transformational deals."

Ezzat said on the earnings call that the group is sharpening its strategic focus around three structural growth themes, AI, Intelligent Operations, and digital sovereignty. These themes will be supported by selective merger and acquisitions (M&A), disciplined investment and a faster shift in skills and delivery model.

He argued that 2026 will be the "moment of truth" for enterprise AI, as clients move beyond proofs of concept and demand measurable outcomes embedded in core operations.

Adoption, he said, is constrained by missing foundations, including modern infrastructure, high-quality data, and standardised governance, risk and compliance frameworks, as well as fragmented legacy systems and the challenge of building trust in human-AI collaboration.

Capgemini's opportunity, he said, is to manage this complexity through domain expertise, transformation capability and partner ecosystems.

Ezzat cited an end-to-end procurement transformation using agentic AI across market intelligence, sourcing, tender analysis, cost simulation, forecasting, contract drafting and value tracking, which has already delivered reported savings of €27m.

He also highlighted a physics-informed AI solution to improve data-centre reliability, integrated into existing workflows, which has helped avoid around 50 critical incidents per year.

On Intelligent Operations, he said the [WNS acquisition](https://www.verdict.co.uk/capgemini-acquiring-wns-for-3-3bn/) strengthens vertical and operational expertise, with integration on track and benefits expected in H2. He reiterated targeted end-2027 synergies and highlighted 100 cross-selling opportunities, a growing pipeline and a first "mega deal" above €600m based on an agentic AI-led transformation and a non-full-time equivalent (FTE) model.

On sovereignty, he pointed to Cloud4C, a planned European-hosted "mirror" platform, Bleu with Orange, and new partnerships with Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, and SAP.

args.summary:
This Yahoo Finance article (originally published by Verdict, a GlobalData brand) reports on Capgemini's full-year 2025 financial results and 2026 outlook.

Key financial results for 2025:
- Net profit attributable to the group fell 4.2% to €1.6bn (down from €1.67bn in 2024; the headline cites ~$1.9bn).
- Revenue rose to €22.5bn, up 1.7% year-over-year (from €22bn); growth was 3.4% at constant exchange rates, surpassing projections.
- Basic EPS fell 3.7% to €9.46; normalised EPS rose 5.8% to €12.95.
- Bookings totalled €24.4bn ($28.96bn), up 3.9% at constant rates, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.08.
- Operating margin stable at 13.3% of revenues (€2.98bn); organic free cash flow of €1.95bn, stable year-over-year.
- Q4 revenue grew 10.6%, driven by cloud, data, AI, and digital business process services, with generative and agentic AI comprising over 10% of Q4 bookings. Q4 growth was supported by the strategic acquisition of WNS, which enhances AI-powered intelligent operations capabilities.

2026 outlook and strategy:
- Revenue growth target of 6.5%–8.5% at constant exchange rates; operating margin projected between 13.6% and 13.8%.
- Restructuring costs of ~€700m anticipated over the next two years to align workforce with growth agenda.
- Strategic focus on three structural growth themes: AI, Intelligent Operations, and digital sovereignty.

Regional performance:
- North America: +7.3% (boosted by WNS and financial services).
- UK & Ireland: +10.5%.
- France: -4.1% due to manufacturing sector challenges.

Headcount: Reached 423,400 as of December 31, 2025, up 82,300 (24%) year-over-year, including an increase of 68,700 since end of September 2025 largely due to WNS integration.

CEO commentary: Aiman Ezzat stated the company exceeded its revenue growth objective while meeting margin and cash flow targets. He called 2026 the "moment of truth" for enterprise AI as clients move beyond proofs of concept. He highlighted examples including an agentic AI procurement transformation that delivered €27m in reported savings, and a physics-informed AI solution for data-centre reliability that avoids ~50 critical incidents per year. On Intelligent Operations, he noted WNS integration is on track with ~100 cross-selling opportunities and a first "mega deal" above €600m. On sovereignty, he highlighted Cloud4C, a planned European-hosted "mirror" platform, Bleu with Orange, and new partnerships with Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, and SAP.

***Paris, October 28, 2025 –*** The [Capgemini](https://www.capgemini.com/) Group reported consolidated revenues of €5,393 million in Q3 2025, up +0.3% year-on-year on a reported basis, and up +2.9% at constant exchange rates\*.

Aiman Ezzat, Chief Executive Officer of the Capgemini Group, said: *“The Group delivered a strong Q3, better than expected, thanks to the relevance of our AI-powered business and technology partner positioning and the targeted actions initiated a year ago, in a demand environment that is largely unchanged. Revenue growth improved in all regions, with a significant acceleration in North America. Demand continued to be driven by cloud, data and AI, with a strong focus on efficiency and optimization.*

*We are accelerating the integration of generative AI across our service portfolio to enable clients to achieve tangible business value. Our investments in proprietary platforms, delivery frameworks, and talent – combined with strategic partnerships – position us as a leader in AI. This is reflected in robust deal wins in generative and agentic-AI.*

*With the acquisition of WNS now complete, we lead in the fast-growing Intelligent Operations market addressing client demand for agentic AI-powered business operations.*

*On the back of this strong performance, we raise our growth target for 2025 to between +2.0% and +2.5% – as a reminder, this is above the top-end of the growth outlook communicated in February 2025[**[1]**](#_ftn2) – and narrow our operating margin target to between 13.3% and 13.4%.*”

|  |  |  |

| **Revenues** | **2024** | **2025** |  | **At current  exchange rates** | **At constant  exchange rates\*** |

Capgemini generated **revenues** of €5,393 million in Q3 2025, up +0.3% year-on-year on a reported basis. In an economic environment that remains uncertain, Capgemini continued to benefit from the targeted actions implemented over the last twelve months. As a result, at constant exchange rates, year-on-year revenue growth improved in Q3 in most regions, businesses and sectors, lifting the Group’s revenue growth from +0.7% in Q2 to +2.9% in Q3 2025.

For the first nine months of the year, revenues grew +1.0% at constant exchange rates and were essentially stable at -0.1% on a reported basis.

The overall demand environment remains stable, with clients continuing to invest selectively in initiatives that support operational efficiency and strategic transformation rather than growth-oriented programs. There is consistent interest in technology-led solutions that deliver tangible outcomes with sustained demand for cloud, digital core, data estate modernization and AI/GenAI solutions.

**Bookings** totaled €5,161 million in Q3 2025, an increase of +1.5% at constant exchange rates, leading to a book-to-bill ratio of 0.96 for the period in line with traditional seasonality.

#### **OPERATIONS BY REGION**

At constant exchange rates, revenues in the **North America** region (28% of 2024 Group revenues) rose +7.0% year-on-year. Growth was driven by the Financial Services and TMT (Telecoms, Media and Technology) sectors as well as the Manufacturing sector, notably in the Life Sciences industry.

Revenues in the **United Kingdom and Ireland** region (12% of 2024 Group revenues) grew by +9.0%. This robust growth was broad-based, with Financial Services and TMT sectors recording the strongest performance.

Revenues in **France** (20% of 2024 Group revenues) declined by -4.7%, notably driven by the persisting weakness in the Manufacturing sector.

Revenues in the **Rest of Europe** region (31% of 2024 Group revenues) decreased by -1.5%. Solid growth in the Public, Consumer Goods & Retail and Financial Services sectors were more than offset by the softness in the Manufacturing and Services sectors.

Finally, revenues in the **Asia-Pacific and Latin America** region (9% of 2024 Group revenues) increased by +13.6%. Growth was particularly robust across the Financial Services, Manufacturing, Energy & Utilities and TMT sectors.

#### **OPERATIONS BY BUSINESS**

At constant exchange rates, total revenues\* of **Strategy & Transformation** services (9% of 2024 Group revenues) were slightly up by +0.7% year-on-year.

**Applications & Technology** services (62% of 2024 Group revenues and Capgemini’s core business) posted a solid growth of +5.7% of their total revenues.

Lastly, **Operations & Engineering** (29% of 2024 Group revenues) total revenues increased by +1.3%, with continued strong growth in Business Services.

#### **HEADCOUNT**

The Group’s total headcount stands at 354,700 as at September 30, 2025, up +4.7% year-on-year. The offshore workforce stands at 211,800 employees or 60% of the total headcount.

#### **OUTLOOK**

The Group’s financial targets for 2025 are updated as follows:

* Revenue growth of +2.0% to +2.5% at constant currency (was -1.0% to +1.0%);
* Operating margin of 13.3% to 13.4% (was 13.3% to 13.5%);
* Organic free cash flow of around €1.9 billion (unchanged).

Following the completion of the acquisition of WNS, the contribution from M&A to revenue growth is now estimated to around 2 points (was around 1 point).

#### **BUSINESS CLASSIFICATION**

* **Strategy & Transformation** includes all strategy, innovation and transformation consulting services.
* **Applications & Technology** brings together “Application Services” and related activities and notably local technology services.
* **Operations & Engineering** encompasses all other Group businesses. These comprise Business Services (including Business Process Outsourcing and transaction services), all Infrastructure and Cloud services, and R&D and Engineering services.

#### **DEFINITIONS**

**Year-on-year revenue growth at constant exchange rates** is calculated by comparing revenues for the reported period with those of the same period of the previous year restated with the exchange rates of the reported period.

|  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Reconciliation of growth rates** | **Q1 2025** | **Q2 2025** | **Q3** **2025** | **9M** **2025** |
| **Growth at constant exchange rates** | **-0.4%** | **+0.7%** | **+2.9%** | **+1.0%** |

| **Reported growth** | **+0.5%** | **-1.0%** | **+0.3%** | **-0.1%** |

When determining activity trends by business and in accordance with internal operating performance measures, growth at constant exchange rates is calculated based on **total revenues**, i.e., before elimination of inter-business billing. The Group considers this to be more representative of activity levels by business. As its businesses change, an increasing number of contracts require a range of business expertise for delivery, leading to a rise in inter-business flows.

**Operating margin** is one of the Group’s key performance indicators. It is defined as the difference between revenues and operating costs. It is calculated before “Other operating income and expenses” which include amortization of intangible assets recognized in business combinations, expenses relative to share-based compensation (including social security contributions and employer contributions) and employee share ownership plan, and non-recurring revenues and expenses, notably impairment of goodwill, negative goodwill, capital gains or losses on disposals of consolidated companies or businesses, restructuring costs incurred under a detailed formal plan approved by the Group’s management, the cost of acquiring and integrating companies acquired by the Group, including earn-outs comprising conditions of presence, and the effects of curtailments, settlements and transfers of defined benefit pension plans.

Normalized net profit is equal to profit for the year (Group share) adjusted for the impact of items recognized in “Other operating income and expense”, net of tax calculated using the effective tax rate. **Normalized earnings per share** is computed like basic earnings per share, i.e., excluding dilution.

**Organic free cash flow** is equal to cash flow from operations less acquisitions of property, plant, equipment and intangible assets (net of disposals) and repayments of lease liabilities, adjusted for cash out relating to the net interest cost.

**Net debt** (or **net cash**) comprises (i) cash and cash equivalents, as presented in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows (consisting of short-term investments and cash at bank) less bank overdrafts, and also including (ii) cash management assets (assets presented separately in the Consolidated Statement of Financial Position due to their characteristics), less (iii) short- and long-term borrowings. Account is also taken of (iv) the impact of hedging instruments when these relate to borrowings, intercompany loans, and own shares.

(Reuters) - French IT consulting group Capgemini on Friday posted higher half-year revenue, driven by its cloud, data and artificial intelligence (AI) activities, and said it would invest 2 billion euros ($2.19 billion) in AI over three years.

The Paris-based company tries to help businesses to adopt AI technology through partnerships with Microsoft and Google Cloud.

"We continue to gain market share as we accompany our clients in their transition towards a digital and sustainable economy ... I am convinced that generative AI will play a major role in this transition," CEO Aiman Ezzat said in a statement.

Generative AI, an increasingly powerful form of AI able to generate on its own text, images, and other content, has become popular since the release of OpenAI’s ChatGPT chatbot last November, increasing concerns over issues such as copyright, cybersecurity, privacy and AI replacing human jobs.

Capgemini, which offers consulting, digital, technical and engineering services, reported revenue of 11.43 billion euros in the first half of 2023, compared to 10.69 billion a year earlier.

The company reiterated its 2023 outlook for revenue growth of between 4% to 7% at constant currency basis.

($1 = 0.9117 euros)

(Reporting by Lina Golovnya and Stéphanie Hamel in Gdansk; Editing by Milla Nissi)

# Capgemini's AI strategy wins over investors despite 13% profit drop

By [Derek du Preez](/author/ddpreez "View user profile.")   ![Profile picture for user ddpreez](/sites/default/files/styles/square_28/public/user/2025-11/1715037520166.jpeg.webp?itok=IEsfC3Gn)   July 30, 2025

Summary:
:   Capgemini's stock surged 6% despite a 13% profit drop as investors focused on the IT services giant's AI strategy, which contributed over 7% of Q2 bookings and positions the company for future growth in artificial intelligence services.

* [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop)
* [Linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop&title=Capgemini%27s%20AI%20strategy%20wins%20over%20investors%20despite%2013%25%20profit%20drop)
* [Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop&title=Capgemini%27s%20AI%20strategy%20wins%20over%20investors%20despite%2013%25%20profit%20drop)
* [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Capgemini%27s%20AI%20strategy%20wins%20over%20investors%20despite%2013%25%20profit%20drop&url=https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop)
* [Threads](https://www.threads.net/intent/post?text=Capgemini%27s%20AI%20strategy%20wins%20over%20investors%20despite%2013%25%20profit%20drop https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop)
* [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/intent/compose?text=Capgemini%27s%20AI%20strategy%20wins%20over%20investors%20despite%2013%25%20profit%20drop https%3A%2F%2Fdiginomica.com%2Fcapgeminis-ai-strategy-wins-over-investors-despite-13-profit-drop)

![Capgemini logo](/sites/default/files/styles/scaled_370/public/images/2014-04/Capgemini-logo1.png.webp?itok=aWJ0WR2P)

Sometimes Wall Street has a funny way of rewarding companies - and it seems that as long as AI is at the forefront, your share price will be protected. This week Capgemini's shares surged 6 percent following earnings that showed a steep 13% decline in net profit, but investors were clearly focused on something else: the French IT services giant's growing traction in Artificial Intelligence (AI).

The earnings themselves painted a mixed picture. Net profit fell to €724 million in the first half of 2025, down from €835 million a year earlier. Revenue, however, managed to edge slightly ahead of internal expectations at €11.1 billion - a modest 0.2 percent increase at constant currency that suggests the company's sales execution remains solid even as profitability takes a hit.

What caught the market's attention was CEO Aiman Ezzat saying that generative AI and agentic AI contributed to more than 7 percent of Q2 bookings. In an environment where most IT services firms are struggling to find growth, that figure represents promise.

## **AI investment**

Capgemini has been betting heavily on AI capabilities, rolling out its Resonance AI Framework and enhancing platforms with new AI agent functionality. The investments appear to be translating into real client wins, with Ezzat citing projects that have delivered measurable outcomes - including one engagement that helped a global life sciences client reduce compliance reporting time "from several weeks to minutes."

However, interestingly, clients are also increasingly expecting to share in AI-driven productivity gains through reduced pricing rather than allowing providers to capture all those efficiencies as improved margins. As Ezzat acknowledges:

"New clients embed or ask for some of the [savings], of course.

It's an interesting dynamic and one that could have consequences for how these services firms price themselves - customers clearly believe that if the AI is good enough, some of the operational savings should be passed on to them too. 

## **Regional divergence**

The geographic breakdown reveals just how uneven the current business environment remains. North America showed improvement with 1.6 percent growth, driven primarily by financial services and telecommunications spending. The UK and Ireland region delivered particularly strong performance with 6 percent growth.

France proved more challenging, declining 5 percent year-over-year despite representing 20% of group revenues. Ezzat characterized the weakness as broader than sector-specific issues, pointing to reduced business confidence and activity levels that have dampened client spending patterns.

Highlighting what he described as "a very competitive pricing environment”, Ezzat notes: 

> We have some of our Indian peers who are shrinking year on year.

Operating margins held steady at 12.4% of revenues, though the profit decline was driven largely by increased restructuring costs, which nearly tripled to €136 million from €53 million in the prior year.

## **Cautious optimism**

Despite the near-term headwinds, Capgemini's board approved a substantial $2 billion multi-year share buyback program, signaling confidence in the company's cash generation capabilities. The program will be funded primarily through organic free cash flow, suggesting management believes the current challenges are manageable.

The company has narrowed its full-year revenue guidance to between -1% and +1% at constant currency, tightening the range from the previous -2% to +2%. Management maintained its operating margin target of 13.3% to 13.5% and organic free cash flow objective of around €1.9 billion.

Ezzat struck a measured tone about the outlook: 

> Going into Q3, we see some stability in the environment, while we retain our cautious stance to account for the uncertainty created by geopolitical tensions and a slow economy.

## **My take**

The market's response to Capgemini's results underscores a broader shift in how investors evaluate enterprise technology companies. Traditional financial metrics still matter, but strategic positioning in emerging technologies like AI has become equally important for valuation.

For Capgemini, the challenge now lies in sustaining its AI momentum while competitors including IBM, Accenture, and major Indian service providers pour resources into similar capabilities. The company's 7 percent AI contribution to bookings represents early validation of its strategy, but maintaining that edge will require continued investment and execution.

The real test will come as economic conditions stabilize and clients move beyond cost optimization to growth-oriented technology spending. Companies that have built genuine AI capabilities during this challenging period may find themselves well-positioned for the next cycle. Whether Capgemini can translate its current AI investments into sustained competitive advantage remains the key question for investors weighing the stock's recent surge.

  For decades, organizations have been trained to think about technology in one way — use it to reimagine enterprise and departmental processes. Every new wave of innovation has followed that same pattern: analyze, redesign, implement, and scale. Sometimes it works brilliantly. Other times, organizational complexity and legacy systems get in the way. But Generative and Agentic AI invite a different way of thinking. Instead of starting with enterprise processes, what if we started with people? Every individual in an organization has their own “personal process” — the way they get things done to meet the demands of their role. Agentic AI can enhance those micro-processes right away, boosting productivity without waiting for massive redesigns or new platforms. By taking a role-based design approach, organizations can build agents that are reusable across similar or adjacent roles — creating powerful network effects and accelerating adoption. I explore this idea more deeply in my article, “Role-based design is key to scaling AI in the enterprise”, where I share examples of how this approach is already driving impact across industries. [https://lnkd.in/em2J86Hj](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2Fem2J86Hj&urlhash=L6bF&trk=public_post-text) Of course there are cases where an approach focused on enterprise process is more appropriate (e.g., when you want to compress time to complete process end-to-end). But pairing that with a role-level strategy can dramatically increase both the speed and scale of AI adoption.   Every industry faces friction at the intersection of tech, process, and people. Role-based AI turns those pain points into opportunities for real progress. Great article by [Edward R. Merchant](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edmerchant?trk=public_post-text)

  [Edward R. Merchant](https://www.linkedin.com/in/edmerchant?trk=public_post_reshare_feed-actor-name)

  Managing Partner & Global Head, BFS Consulting | Change Agent for the AI Era | Driving Transformation at the Intersection of Industry, Technology & Human Ingenuity

  For decades, organizations have been trained to think about technology in one way — use it to reimagine enterprise and departmental processes. Every new wave of innovation has followed that same pattern: analyze, redesign, implement, and scale. Sometimes it works brilliantly. Other times, organizational complexity and legacy systems get in the way. But Generative and Agentic AI invite a different way of thinking. Instead of starting with enterprise processes, what if we started with people? Every individual in an organization has their own “personal process” — the way they get things done to meet the demands of their role. Agentic AI can enhance those micro-processes right away, boosting productivity without waiting for massive redesigns or new platforms. By taking a role-based design approach, organizations can build agents that are reusable across similar or adjacent roles — creating powerful network effects and accelerating adoption. I explore this idea more deeply in my article, “Role-based design is key to scaling AI in the enterprise”, where I share examples of how this approach is already driving impact across industries. [https://lnkd.in/em2J86Hj](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=https%3A%2F%2Flnkd%2Ein%2Fem2J86Hj&urlhash=L6bF&trk=public_post_reshare-text) Of course there are cases where an approach focused on enterprise process is more appropriate (e.g., when you want to compress time to complete process end-to-end). But pairing that with a role-level strategy can dramatically increase both the speed and scale of AI adoption.   Deploying AI agents in an enterprise setting poses unique challenges that go beyond the initial excitement surrounding their capabilities. While it may seem straightforward to implement AI solutions, several key factors contribute to the complexity and potential failure of AI agent deployment within an organization. 1. \*\*Choosing the Right Solution\*\*: Not every problem requires the sophistication of Agentic AI. It's essential to discern when simpler approaches like code-based solutions, traditional machine learning, or basic automation tools are more suitable. Opting for an AI agent just because it's marketed as cutting-edge can lead to unnecessary complications. Reserve AI agents for intricate, multi-step workflows where adaptability is paramount. 2. \*\*Defining Workflows\*\*: Clarity in workflow understanding is crucial before automation. Enterprises often grapple with convoluted processes that lack transparency. Prior to automation, dissect the workflow to identify manual components and determine what can feasibly be automated with Agentic AI. Without a clear workflow strategy, automation efforts risk targeting the wrong areas, resulting in low adoption rates or project abandonment. 3. \*\*System Integration Challenges\*\*: Integrating AI agents into existing legacy systems presents a significant hurdle. Many legacy systems were not designed with AI compatibility in mind, complicating the integration process. Connecting to APIs is just the tip of the iceberg; navigating through years of technical debt, isolated data silos, and fragile interdependencies is a formidable task. A smoothly running demo on a new system can quickly unravel in a complex enterprise environment where legacy systems reign. 4. \*\*Thorough Evaluation\*\*: The efficacy of AI agents must be rigorously evaluated across various performance metrics. Assessment should occur at task and workflow levels, ensuring alignment with business objectives such as time savings and cost reduction. Safety metrics are equally critical to prevent unintended consequences. Without robust evaluation protocols, AI agents risk either underperforming in real-world scenarios post-demonstration or causing unforeseen disruptions without detection. Successfully deploying AI agents in an enterprise demands a holistic approach that considers the nuances of the organization's workflows,. This webpage is a LinkedIn post by Andreas Sjostrom (an Influencer with ~14,000 followers) discussing how AI is moving from hype to measurable business impact, using Capgemini's Q2 2025 results as evidence. Key highlights include:
- More than 7% of Capgemini's Q2 bookings were tied to AI and Generative AI initiatives.
- Client outcomes: media companies using AI agents to automate finance operations; energy clients modernizing legacy apps with GenAI; life sciences compressing ISO-compliant reporting from weeks to minutes (protecting billions in annual revenue); aerospace clients using AI-powered design to reduce production non-conformities.
- Capgemini's strategic assets: Resonance AI Framework, AI-first portfolio, and the RAISE platform (featuring AI agents, GenAI assistants, and multi-agent orchestration).
- Conclusion that AI is about execution at scale; winners embed AI into business models, combine domain expertise with AI platforms, and translate innovation into financial impact.

The page also contains several "More Relevant Posts" from other LinkedIn authors:
1. Lewis Walker summarizing Bain's 2025 Technology Report (77 pages, 11 topics) covering AI agents, sovereign tech fragmentation, compute power demand, humanoid robots, quantum computing, agentic AI's impact on SaaS, and generative AI in software development.
2. Robert Rogowski's post with key Bain report quotes: AI leaders deliver 10%-25% EBITDA gains; top tech firms (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Nvidia) capture over 70% of AI market value; $500B annual capex needed for AI data centers by 2030; AI compute demand growth exceeds 2x Moore's law; early adopters see >30% win-rate improvement in sales.
3. Javier Pozuelo on Cognizant's Neuro Generative AI Adoption approach (identifying high-impact use cases, multi-agent orchestration, responsible implementation with ISO 42001:2023 certification).

7. ArunKumar R on challenges of deploying AI agents in enterprises (choosing the right solution, defining workflows, system integration, thorough evaluation).

Company Profile

Capgemini Group was founded in 1967 and is one of the world's most renowned providers of management consulting, technology, and outsourcing services. The company is listed on the Paris Stock Exchange and is a constituent of prominent indices such as the Dow Jones & Company STOXX and the Dow Jones Euro STOXX.

Core Business

Consulting services, technology services, and outsourcing services are Capgemini's three core businesses. The company's goal is to comprehensively enhance clients' performance and competitiveness through fully integrated, end-to-end solutions delivered via these three service lines.

Capgemini's experts specialize in providing solutions for issues arising from strategic, market, supply chain operations, personnel, and technological changes in the Digital Economy. Leveraging Capgemini's professional insights and acumen in Electronic Information and business transformation, it offers strategic transformation consulting and IT strategy planning. It provides relevant management consulting in areas such as Customer Relationship Management, Supply chain management, finance and human resources transformation, and digital transformation. It designs and delivers winning strategies for clients, helping them significantly improve their performance.

Technology Services: Driving Innovation and Gaining Full Control of the IT Environment

By utilizing Capgemini's Accelerated Solutions Environment, Rapid Innovation (RAIN) methodology, and global network of Accelerated Delivery Centers, it significantly reduces the time required to execute IT strategies. Outsourcing Services: Pursuing Faster, More Sustainable Performance

Enterprises rely on consulting firms to help them solve their most complex business problems. Capgemini's innovative right-shoring approach helps clients optimally utilize the most suitable combination of human resources. Simultaneously, Capgemini's Collaborative Business Experience flexibly adapts to clients' unique business needs: from traditional optimization of IT cost structures to value-added transformational layouts, it delivers maximum profit enhancement for clients.

Industry Clients

While Capgemini integrates its three core businesses—consulting services, technology services, and outsourcing services—across all industries, it also focuses its services on four key sectors based on market and client needs: Energy, Utilities & Chemical Industry; Engineering & Construction; Financial Services; and Manufacturing & Retail. It provides end-to-end solutions for these four key industries. 64% of the Fortune Global 500 companies are Capgemini's clients.

Energy, Utilities and Chemicals Industry

Manufacturing, Retail, and Logistics & Transportation

Collaborative Business Experience™

Capgemini at your side: Implementing a people-centric approach to technology application to create tangible and effective business outcomes

Starts with people, ends with results

With technological advancement, geographical boundaries are gradually disappearing, and competition is becoming increasingly fierce. For enterprises to succeed, they increasingly need to be prepared to respond to complex, volatile, and unpredictable challenges at any moment. Capgemini's team of experts is dedicated to serving clients, striving to enhance their flexibility and competitiveness.

Finding unique solutions together

Collaboration in Action

Capgemini is a favored partner for well-known enterprises across various industries. The company's client success stories demonstrate how the Collaborative Business Experience™ helps businesses improve performance through innovation in a more agile manner.

Based on over 30 years of experience working with thousands of companies, Capgemini has summarized the following four essential elements of collaboration. Together, they form a picture that reveals an enterprise's strengths, weaknesses, needs, and priorities. They help Capgemini actively collaborate with clients to achieve better, faster, and more sustainable outcomes.

Setting Target Value

To improve performance, it is essential to clearly define what is desired, then set targets aligned with the project's trajectory.

Reducing Risk

The success or failure of a project is a major concern. This element reflects Capgemini's understanding of the critical factors for business opportunities and the level of associated risk perceived by the client. It enables Capgemini to Risk management, reducing the likelihood of obstacles to value realization.

Optimizing Capabilities

This element signifies a two-way exchange of knowledge within the project and the joint effort required by Capgemini and the client to determine how to provide support to ensure the project's value is appropriately applied to the business.

Coordinate the entire organization

Many business opportunities fail to deliver sustained value due to implementation failures or internal delays within the company. This outcome can stem from various causes. Mission

Capgemini: It starts with people and is accomplished through endeavors, jointly fostering the integration of management philosophy and technological practice.

The company's vision: Tailoring endeavors to people.

Capgemini has always believed that relying solely on technological power cannot achieve genuine business value. The creation of value is akin to a vital force; it starts with people and is accomplished through endeavors. From the outset of delivering solutions that best fit business needs, Capgemini experts work with clients to analyze the core of each business requirement. Capgemini firmly believes that tailoring endeavors to people will achieve distinctive business value.

Capgemini helps enterprises achieve organizational transformation and improve efficiency. By accurately and effectively combining enterprise capabilities with matching technologies, it helps clients enhance business agility, making enterprises more competitive.

Collaboration is the core business philosophy of Capgemini. The company's experts and clients jointly form collaborative teams. Capgemini's unique form of collaborative cooperation is called the Collaborative Business Experience®. The company collaboratively creates and delivers technology and business solutions that meet client needs and achieve business value.

Values

Employees hired by Capgemini should identify with the following seven fundamental values:

Honesty

Loyalty, honesty, integrity, and never using any underhanded means to win business or gain an advantage. Growth, profitability, and independence have no real value unless they are achieved through complete honesty and integrity. Teams should be deeply aware that if the company lacks openness and integrity, its business will be immediately damaged.

Courage

Courage means the ability to lead an enterprise and the determination to consider risks and take responsibility (naturally establishing a firm resolve to fulfill one's duties). This is the soul of competition: firmly making decisions and driving their implementation, regularly making commitments, and challenging one's own future and the status quo. Courage also requires a degree of prudence and particularly clear vision. Otherwise, any bold manager is merely recklessly courting danger.

Trust

Trust means the willingness to delegate authority to individuals or teams; making decisions as close to the point of action as possible. Trust also implies genuine openness and broad information sharing with employees within the company.

Freedom

Freedom means independence in thought, judgment, action, entrepreneurship, and creativity. It also means tolerance and respect for different cultures and customs: essential qualities for a team composed of over 83,000 employees from thirty or forty different countries.

Team Spirit

Team spirit is the embodiment of camaraderie, loyalty, tolerance, and fairness when sharing the benefits of collective creation; it is about taking responsibility and expressing a clear willingness to support common efforts when risks arise.

Modesty

Modesty is unadorned, the opposite of hypocrisy, conceit, ostentation, arrogance, and boastfulness. Unadorned does not mean naive (simple does not mean foolish); it is more about prudence, demonstrating natural humility, sound judgment, attentiveness to others, and taking the trouble to be fully understood. In work relationships, modesty manifests as frankness, ease, and a sense of humor.

Joy

This means feeling good as a member of the company or team, taking pride in the actions of others, experiencing a sense of accomplishment in the pursuit of better quality and higher efficiency, and feeling part of challenging projects.

The company has established a formal ethical charter to articulate and promote these practices, which define how the company collaborates with clients and interacts with its employees.

Historical Review

Since its founding in 1967, Capgemini has gradually developed into one of the world's top five IT services and consulting companies. Over the past 40 years, the company has witnessed successes, accepted challenges, and undergone repositioning.

New Development Strategy (1990-1997)

Capgemini established a world-class management consulting practice through a series of strategic acquisitions, including the purchase of United Research in the US in 1990, Mac Group in the US in 1991, Gruber Titze and Partners in Europe in 1993, and Bossard in Europe in 1997.

Building the Future (1998-)

Capgemini is a Paris-based global IT services and consulting company founded in 1967 by Serge Kampf. It is a CAC 40 constituent, operating in 39 countries, with over 125,000 employees (as of the mid-2010s profile data) and revenue exceeding €10.3 billion in 2012. It ranked 214th on the Global 500 Brand Value Ranking in 2024 and 484th on the Forbes Global 2000 in 2021.

**Core Business:** Capgemini's three core businesses are Consulting Services, Technology Services, and Outsourcing Services. Its service model is the "Collaborative Business Experience" — a people-centric approach emphasizing four elements: setting target value, reducing risk, optimizing capabilities, and coordinating the entire organization. Its key industry focuses include Energy/Utilities/Chemicals, Financial Services (serving 80% of the world's top 30 financial institutions), Manufacturing/Retail (14 of the world's 15 largest auto manufacturers), and Government/Public Services. 64% of the Fortune Global 500 companies are its clients. Capgemini entered China in 1997 and operates in Hangzhou, Shanghai, Beijing, Guangzhou, Kunshan, Hong Kong, and Taipei with over 1,600 consultants, serving primarily large Chinese state-owned enterprises.

**Key Values:** The company's seven fundamental values are honesty, courage, trust, freedom, team spirit, modesty, and joy.

- **July 2025:** Capgemini research found 93% of surveyed business leaders believed large-scale AI Agent deployment within 12 months would bring competitive advantage; projected Agents could generate up to $450 billion in economic value by 2028.
- **August 2025:** Announced acquisition of hybrid cloud platform provider Cloud4C.
- **December 2025:** Named by the U.S. Trade Representative in a warning over EU regulation of U.S. tech giants; secured a $4.8 million data analytics contract with U.S. ICE.

args.summary:
This LinkedIn post from Entrepreneur Media India (246,819 followers) reports on Capgemini's strategic acquisitions to strengthen its digital capabilities in AI and cloud computing.

**Key facts:**
- **Cloud4C acquisition**: Announced August 2025, Capgemini agreed to acquire 100% ownership of Singapore-based Cloud4C Services Pte Ltd and Cloud4C Services Pvt Ltd by Capgemini SE. Cloud4C is a leader in hybrid cloud platform and managed cloud services. The Competition Commission of India (CCI) approved the acquisition to ensure fair competition.
- **WNS acquisition**: In July 2025 (announced), Capgemini agreed to acquire WNS Global Services for $3.3 billion (₹27,500+ crore), excluding debt. WNS brings strong Business Process Management (BPM) and Intelligent Operations expertise with deep process skills in insurance, travel, healthcare, finance, customer experience, and analytics, with over 44,000 employees in India.
  - Timeline: Deal announced July 2025; WNS shareholders approved Aug 29, 2025; acquisition completed October 17, 2025.
  - WNS contributes 9% average revenue growth and 18.7% margins.
  - Expected to boost Capgemini's EPS by 4% (2026) and 7% (2027 post-synergies).
- **Capgemini CEO Aiman Ezzat** stated the deals will help the company leverage AI and scale its services.
- Capgemini is a French IT firm headquartered in Paris, a global leader in consulting, digital transformation, technology, and engineering services, operating in 50+ countries with a combined workforce of 400,000+.
- The combined entity creates a global leader in Agentic AI-powered Intelligent Operations.

**Analyst caution**: D.D. Mishra of Gartner cautioned that successful acquisitions require careful integration, cultural alignment, and sustained focus on internal innovation to avoid common pitfalls.

**Related content on the page:**
- **Atos** faces challenges with falling revenue due to key contract losses; after a financial overhaul, it's focusing on defense and high-performance computing under CEO Philippe Salle, with acquisitions paused until 2026.
- **SoftwareOne** completed its $1.5 billion acquisition of Crayon Group in July 2025, creating one of the world's largest cloud/software providers with 13,000+ employees in 70+ countries and ~CHF 1.6 billion annual revenues, targeting CHF 80-100 million in annual cost efficiencies.
- **Accenture** cut 11,419 employees in the September 2025 quarter as part of restructuring, bringing global headcount to ~770,000, while investing in AI-led transformation.

# Capgemini Acquires WNS For US$3.3bn in Agentic AI Push

![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/138/e585b486ab6024c3a0dfe3da49286d16:83d4e7afa35b5de7ec0ccb2e51c751a8/handshake-blue-line.webp)

[Capgemini](https://technologymagazine.com/company/capgemini) has announced it is paying US$3.3bn to acquire business transformation and services company WNS as companies continue to replace human workers with [AI agents](https://aimagazine.com/articles/globant-how-agentic-ai-is-transforming-business-operations) in their back offices.

The acquisition creates a €23.3 billion entity targeting what both companies call “intelligent operations”: business processes managed by AI systems that can make decisions and adapt without human oversight.

## The death of traditional outsourcing

“Enterprises are rapidly adopting Generative AI and Agentic AI to transform their operations end-to-end,” says Aiman Ezzat, CEO of Capgemini. “Business Process Services will be the showcase for Agentic AI. Capgemini’s acquisition of WNS will provide the Group with the scale and vertical sector expertise to capture that rapidly-emerging strategic opportunity created by the paradigm shift from traditional BPS to Agentic AI-powered Intelligent Operations.”

The deal reflects a shift in how companies approach business process outsourcing. Traditional labour-intensive services are being replaced by [AI-driven automation](https://technologymagazine.com/articles/wef-report-the-impact-of-ai-driving-170m-new-jobs-by-2030) that promises not just cost savings but transformational business outcomes. Companies that once sought cheap offshore labour now demand intelligent systems that can adapt, learn and operate with minimal human oversight.

WNS, which generated US$1.266 billion in revenue last year serving clients including United Airlines, Aviva, M&T Bank, Centrica and McCain Foods, has positioned itself at the forefront of this transformation, maintaining constant currency revenue growth of 9% annually over three years and projecting growth of 7% to 11% for fiscal year 2026.

“As a recognised leader in the Digital Business Process Services space, we see the next wave of transformation being driven by intelligent, domain-centric operations that unlock strategic value for our clients,” says Keshav Murugesh, CEO of WNS. “Organisations that have already digitised are now seeking to reimagine their operating models by embedding AI at the core – shifting from automation to autonomy.”

## Capgemini’s AI ambitions

The acquisition addresses Capgemini’s need for scale in the US market while providing access to WNS's industry-specific platforms and domain expertise. Aiman has invested heavily in AI capabilities, establishing 25 strategic partnerships with [technology providers](https://technologymagazine.com/articles/top-10-enterprise-platforms) including Microsoft, Google, AWS, Mistral AI and Nvidia. The company says it reported over €900 million in generative AI bookings during 2024.

Market analysts including Forrester, IDC and ISG have recognised Capgemini’s position in the AI services market. Aiman has developed training programmes and AI-focused service offerings to meet enterprise demand for AI-powered business transformation.

![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dA_RRj5GZJA/hqdefault.jpg)

Capgemini expects the transaction to generate revenue synergies of €100 million to €140 million by the end of 2027, alongside cost synergies of €50 million to €70 million annually. Aiman anticipates 4% accretion to normalised earnings per share before synergies in 2026, rising to 7% post-synergies in 2027.

## Enabling next-generation, data-driven operations

The transaction requires approval from the Royal Court of Jersey and WNS shareholders, alongside regulatory clearances. Both companies’ boards have unanimously approved the acquisition, with closing expected by the end of 2025.

“By combining our deep domain and process expertise with Capgemini’s global reach, cutting-edge Gen AI and Agentic AI capabilities, a robust [partner ecosystem](https://technologymagazine.com/ai-and-machine-learning/rise-platforms-and-digital-ecosystems-sharing-economy) and advanced technology platforms, we are creating a powerful proposition that accelerates enterprise reinvention,” says Keshav. “WNS’ complementary portfolio of horizontal and industry-specific solutions will significantly enhance Capgemini’s rapidly-growing Business Services footprint, enabling next-generation, data-driven operations across sectors.”

The companies expect immediate cross-selling opportunities through the integration of complementary client bases and service offerings, supported by what they describe as natural cultural alignment and shared values.

“Just as importantly, our shared values, cultural alignment and complementary client relationships ensure a seamless integration – unlocking exciting opportunities for innovation, co-creation and growth across all stakeholder groups,” says Keshav.

args.summary:
This is a research brief from the Capgemini Research Institute titled "The multi-year AI advantage: Building the enterprise of tomorrow" (2026). It's designed for senior leaders (CEOs, CXOs) shaping their organizations' AI agenda, based on a global survey of 1,505 senior leaders (director level and above) across 15 countries conducted in November 2025.

Key findings:
- **AI as strategic imperative**: AI is viewed as a long-term strategic imperative rather than experimental. 57% of organizations believe AI will have long-term transformational impact despite short-term uncertainty, though confidence varies by industry (75% in Media down to 52% in Banking). 53% view AI with a 5+ year investment horizon.
- **Investment increases**: AI budgets are set to rise from 3% of annual business budget in 2025 to 5% in 2026. 68% are focused on measurable business outcomes, and 66% believe failing to scale AI risks losing competitive edge.
- **AI winter resilience**: Even in a potential AI winter (2-3 years of declining optimism), organizations plan to continue investing. 80% would shift to foundational capabilities, 72% prioritize high-impact/low-cost initiatives, 64% reassess portfolios, 57% preserve core talent.
- **AI adoption across organization**: Sales & marketing (63%) and IT operations (55%) are top investment hotspots. Gen AI has crossed from pilots to scaled use, with 38% of organizations operationalizing Gen AI (only 2% scaled across most functions, with 43% at pilots/POCs stage). Six in ten organizations are exploring agentic AI (36% piloting or using at global level, with China ahead at 46% vs US 41% and Europe 30%).
- **Edge and physical AI**: Nearly half report limited or full edge AI deployment. Edge AI spending forecast to reach $260 billion in 2025 and $380 billion by 2028. ML leads with 72% expecting major impact in 2026.
- **Build vs. buy**: The approach emphasizes building where it differentiates, buying where it accelerates. 44% primarily buy commercial solutions, 31% primarily build in-house, 14% pivot by use case, 11% buy foundational models but build custom applications. 62% balance open-source and proprietary tools.
- **Scaling enablers**: Strong executive sponsorship (67%), external partnerships (59%), workforce upskilling (53%), governance (53%), regulatory clarity/ethical frameworks (53%), and scalable data infrastructure (51%) are key accelerators.
- **Human-AI chemistry**: 66% confirm human-AI collaboration improved productivity and decision quality; 59% report employees feel empowered to use AI; 48% have clearly defined human/AI roles. AI is seen as amplifying not replacing humans. Trust and human control over critical decisions are essential.
- **Data sovereignty**: 54% prioritize data sovereignty; AI sovereignty emerging as strategic priority.
- **2026 investment priorities**: Data foundations/pipelines (72%), compute/infrastructure (64%), model development/licensing (50%); governance/safety/risk (73%), upskilling (69%), AI centers of excellence (56%).

Notable corporate examples cited: Volkswagen Group ($1.17B AI investment by 2030, targeting €4B savings by 2035), Pfizer (17 Gen AI use cases, $750M-$1B annual savings), Google ($40B through 2027 for cloud/AI infrastructure), Bosch ($2.7B AI investment by 2027), Eli Lilly (in-house AI supercomputing "factory"), Toyota Software Academy, Lockheed Martin's Astris AI subsidiary, OpenAI/NVIDIA partnership (10GW systems, NVIDIA up to $100B investment), AWS India expansion ($7B plus $12.7B by 2030), Qualcomm/EdgeImpulse, Nordic/Neuton.AI, NXP/Kinara edge AI acquisitions.

The report identifies four strategic imperatives: strengthen AI essentials, advance AI readiness through governance, build human-AI chemistry as core capability, and scale AI value balancing "Transform Now" vs "Build Tomorrow."

args.summary:
This webpage describes the Capgemini AI Academy Practitioner's Program, an externally-available corporate training program designed to upskill workforces in artificial intelligence and data science. The program is delivered by Capgemini practitioners to client practitioners, requiring only a laptop and headset to get started. It has already trained over a thousand Capgemini AI experts internally and is now being offered externally.

The program consists of six key course tracks across three levels and functional areas:
- **Data Literacy**: An introductory course (one week, 4 hours) for those new to AI, covering the basics of AI/ML and business problems AI can solve.
- **Professional**: A four-week course (10 hrs/week) building a strong foundation in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and NLP using Python and cloud platforms (Azure ML Services, AWS SageMaker, GCP).
- **Expert**: A four-week continuation (10 hrs/week) exploring advanced concepts of Deep Learning and NLP, including neural networks, CNN, RNN, and custom AI/ML model building on cloud platforms, culminating in a capstone project required for progression.
- **Business Functional**: Business-oriented program establishing the value of data and AI.
- **Business Influencer**: A high-level executive stream (three days, 15 hours) for CXOs and business leaders to formulate and strategize AI/ML projects at enterprise scale.
- **Qualifying**: A technical/professional-level track (three days, 6 hours).

Key features include: mentor-led journeys with constant guidance, customization by sector/function, a blended "best of both worlds" approach balancing practical and academic content, self-paced learning, and continuous content updates informed by participant feedback, Capgemini's in-house research, and automated "AI for AI" techniques. Courses are suitable for employees with both business-focused and technical backgrounds and provide completion certificates at each level.

The program is positioned as addressing workforce digital upskilling needs and helping organizations deliver real-world AI solutions at scale, particularly relevant in the context of the pandemic-driven need for insight-based decision-making. Contact information is provided for Paramita Gupta (Vice President, Insights & Data) and Manik Seth (Senior Director, Insights & Data) at Capgemini. The document is dated 2020.

A tester uses GenAI to think through edge cases and risks. And an architect uses GenAI to make design decisions visible with clear rationale.

GenAI supports these roles by processing large volumes of information, revealing connections, and suggesting possible directions or solutions. How you apply that output depends on the demands of your profession. One role focuses on technical precision, another on coherence of argumentation, risks, creativity, or user behavior. The core of this deepening is learning how GenAI adapts to the way you think and work. ## Re-skilling, up-skilling and cross-skilling IT professionals

**New technology and innovations are being developed at an unprecedented pace. This means that IT roles are constantly changing, while existing digital skills quickly become obsolete. On top of that, we are currently facing a massive shortage of available IT professionals. How do you optimally prepare your organization for the digital transformation while facing such challenges. Our advise: Invest in the digital talent of your current workforce by choosing our SKILLIT programme. ​**

SKILLIT is aimed at strengthening the quality and capacity of the IT professionals within your organization. We don’t just train and develop the existing skills of your current digital talents, but also prepare employees in other professions for an IT role. This way we ensure a future fit and sustainable workforce and a ‘digital first’ organization.

### SKILLIT offers three different learning journeys:

![Twee mannen die met elkaar communiceren op kantoor](https://academy.capgemini.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/Overig_Desktop-Image-830pX500px_05.jpg)

### Reskilling

Reskilling: Employees who do not have a background in IT learn new digital skills in order to prepare them for a future IT role. For example, a financial advisor who is being trained to become a data engineer.​

![medewerker is lachend aan het bellen](https://academy.capgemini.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/800x500-medewerker-is-lachend-aan-het-bellen.png)

### Upskilling

Upskilling: IT professionals learn new digital skills to stay ahead in their own profession or to expand their current role. For example, an IT architect who is trained in SAFe Agile or Scrum. Or a software engineer who is familiarizing himself with a new programming language such as Python or Java.​

![collega's zijn met elkaar in gesprek](https://academy.capgemini.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/830x500-collegas-zijn-met-elkaar-in-gesprek.png)

### Retraining

Retraining (Cross-skilling): IT professionals learn completely new digital skills to prepare for a new future IT role. For example, a business analyst who is retrained to become a DevOps engineer.​

This is how we guarantee a great learning experience and an optimal learning effect:

* Tailor-made learning journeys: In co-creation with our clients and supported by continual evaluation, we design a custom learning path that exactly fits the context of your organization and the development needs of your employees.​
* Quick start: Thanks to our extensive portfolio of IT courses, we can start every project in no time.​
* Flexibility: Due to our iterative and agile way of working, each learning journey is continuously tweaked and optimized to the learning preferences of the participants.​
* Cost efficient: You avoid the uncertainty and high costs of external recruitment, while being guaranteed of fit-for-future employees with extensive knowledge of your organization and industry.​

## Digital and soft skills

In each learning journey, participants are being trained in both soft skills (customer focus, inquisitiveness, flexibility, collaboration and more) and technical skills such as data analysis, cloud computing and web development. To cement these new skills, real life cases from your organization and the daily practice of your employees are incorporated into the training sessions. After completing each learning path, your employees will have the required skills for roles such as software developer, cloud engineer, data engineer, business analyst and DevOps engineer.​

## GenAI training courses at Capgemini Academy

Our training courses are designed not only to teach you the theory of GenAI, but also to show you how to apply these techniques practically in your work. Whether you’re a software engineer, a data professional or other staff, we have an appropriate training course for every target audience.

### Why is GenAI so important?

GenAI, or generative artificial intelligence, makes it possible to automate repetitive tasks and accelerate work processes considerably. Thanks to AI techniques, professionals can work more quickly, track down errors earlier and better optimize processes, allowing more latitude for more complex and creative tasks.

With the emergence of GenAI, new skills are increasingly important, such as effective guidance of AI models (prompt engineering) and critically assessing the output generated. Organizations that embrace GenAI can respond with more flexibility and innovation to changing market conditions.

### What does a GenAI user do in an organization?

Those who master GenAI are able to integrate generative artificial intelligence into disparate processes to improve the efficiency, stability and scalability of technology solutions.

In short, those who master the theory and practice of AI play a vital role in an organization.

### Why take a GenAI training course?

Our GenAI training courses give you practical methods for deploying GenAI effectively so that you can perform your work even better, more productively and efficiently. Regardless of whether this involves automating routine tasks or more specialist skills.

Because GenAI is shaping the future, you as a professional are immersing yourself in skills that will serve you for many years to come.

[October 6, 2025](https://www.facebook.com/implicatorai/posts/pfbid02xmXtPQTdre76szZ5D2sT35bdXZ9CdqNtwWrQWcCLH7TfS9LoK9fFDk7ZehZTkPN8l?__cft__[0]=AZa26_wUnechfTdDxmsIqb3J6DE_fqyBS6OM1HHx_eWSj-8fyX1r1f4h6bZCAbcD_C1DWuMnGvXAw7OHoyXYKK9O14IKg38xt3D9prUbWMqzXPFKVeaBl6_6aRxTydMHxsEWuicy0vpJ-wm6isdf36LnYffCHUSDXxVnTsiGPAqdEw&__tn__=%2CO%2CP-R)  ·

![🔍](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/tc1/1/16/1f50d.png) Anthropic just deployed Claude to 470,000 Deloitte employees across 150+ countries. Everyone sees a big enterprise deal. The real story? This isn't a software contract—it's a distribution machine.

Deloitte serves nearly 90% of the Fortune Global 500. One systems integrator now seeds hundreds of accounts at once, complete with certified staff who recommend Claude by default. For Anthropic, it's the classic "own the channel" play for the AI era.

![📊](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/taa/1/16/1f4ca.png) The numbers everyone missed: Deloitte is certifying 15,000 practitioners on Claude—not just users, but implementation specialists who build custom deployments for clients. That's consulting infrastructure with switching costs baked in. When thousands are trained, workflows are rebuilt, and compliance sign-offs depend on Claude-specific guarantees, procurement can't swap vendors with a pricing email.

This single deployment is larger than most AI vendors' entire customer bases by seat count. It signals the central truth of 2025: heavyweight enterprise wins outweigh consumer buzz. A handful of deals with trained staff and compliance frameworks beat viral growth every time.

![⚡](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/t5d/1/16/26a1.png) What shifts next: Enterprise AI competition moves from product features to integration depth.

OpenAI chases 200+ million weekly consumer users through ChatGPT. Anthropic is betting on deep integration with fewer partners—embedding inside consulting firms that touch hundreds of clients. Different distribution models, same market. OpenAI wants broad adoption. Anthropic wants enterprises willing to train thousands and build custom workflows.

The Deloitte alliance started in 2024, but the scope just expanded: global staff access, role-specific configurations (tax research, code generation, proposal drafts), and a hard push into regulated industries where compliance kills deals. This is where AI contracts live or die—not feature demos, but audit trails and data residency that legal teams can defend.

![💡](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/t3c/1/16/1f4a1.png) The competitive trap nobody's watching: Compliance is becoming the moat.

Anthropic's "safety-first" posture started as philosophy. Now it's a commercial wedge. If Deloitte can ship reference implementations that pass bank and hospital scrutiny, procurement conversations change from "Can we use AI?" to "How fast can we deploy Claude?" That's a lock rivals can't pick with lower token pricing.

Regulated industries need audit trails, policy enforcement, and explainability. General-purpose chatbots with thin governance layers can't compete when risk officers demand named controls and certified integrators. Claude's enterprise pitch isn't "better model"—it's "we'll help you satisfy auditors."

The timing connects: September 2024, Anthropic closed $13 billion at a $183 billion valuation, launched Claude Sonnet 4.5 as its flagship coding/agent model, and committed to tripling international workforce. The cash funds heavy enterprise adoption. The hiring sustains hands-on support. The model release creates sales momentum. The Deloitte rollout turns all three into distribution leverage.

Here's the distribution calculus: Deloitte consultants now have live sandboxes, benchmarks, and Claude artifacts they walk into client meetings. Internal deployment gives them credibility—"we use what we sell"—plus billable follow-ons: persona design, red-teaming, data-guardrail tuning, agent workflow rewrites. That's recurring revenue with lock-in. Once 15,000 people are certified and workflows standardized, rival models might look cheaper per token. They won't be cheaper to replace.

The Center of Excellence isn't marketing fluff. It's an internal team building implementation frameworks, developing role-specific configs, troubleshooting technical issues, and creating reusable templates for client deployments. Think IT help desk meets solution architecture meets change management—designed to prevent AI pilots from stalling in procurement or compliance purgatory. That's where most enterprise deals die. Anthropic and Deloitte are pre-solving the blocker.

Rolling out to 470,000 people isn't a press release—it's change management at scale. Role scoping, red-team testing, access control, cost guardrails, steady training. Deloitte will start with high-leverage lanes like tax research and code generation, then graduate to agentic workflows touching client data. The payoff is big. The blast radius of mistakes is bigger. Move carefully, but move.

Three signals show whether this becomes template or outlier. First: seat activation. How many people move beyond novelty to weekly use. Second: case studies. Regulated clients citing measurable gains with named controls in finance, health, public sector. Third: copycats. Do the other Big Four formalize model-specific Centers of Excellence, or stick with "bring your own LLM"? If Deloitte's flywheel spins, expect a land-grab for channels, not just features.

The strategic bet is clear: Enterprise AI distribution shifts to integrators. The winner won't just have the best model—they'll own…

[![No photo description available.](https://scontent.faju7-1.fna.fbcdn.net/v/t39.30808-6/558306698_122156413472765202_760872103228101678_n.webp?stp=dst-jpg_tt6&cstp=mx1200x800&ctp=p180x540&_nc_cat=102&ccb=1-7&_nc_sid=127cfc&_nc_ohc=VU9Alw1V_kYQ7kNvwH6X3pO&_nc_oc=AdrM1VoUJPq3hKjdF69Ntqsde3J713BKh9m4zdy2Y5kRp1M24fMT5da9rx4tHqdlA7k&_nc_zt=23&_nc_ht=scontent.faju7-1.fna&_nc_gid=6i_RKysn-Y0KUnHBzHVPLQ&_nc_ss=7e289&oh=00_AQExdatcribzoTZSmih6fOXMqA8xP54KeM0C-2zr0av-uA&oe=6A8CE713)](https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=122156413466765202&set=a.122154737408765202&__cft__[0]=AZa26_wUnechfTdDxmsIqb3J6DE_fqyBS6OM1HHx_eWSj-8fyX1r1f4h6bZCAbcD_C1DWuMnGvXAw7OHoyXYKK9O14IKg38xt3D9prUbWMqzXPFKVeaBl6_6aRxTydMHxsEWuicy0vpJ-wm6isdf36LnYffCHUSDXxVnTsiGPAqdEw&__tn__=EH-R)

# Why Anthropic is Bringing Claude to 470k Deloitte Employees

By[James Darley](/author/james-darley)

October 07, 2025

This is Anthropic's largest-ever enterprise IT deal | Credit: Anthropic

Anthropic's Claude AI model is being rolled out to 470,000 Deloitte employees as the start-up expands its partnerships with major firms like Slack & IBM

[Anthropic](https://technologymagazine.com/news/a-moment-of-reckoning-inside-anthropics-landmark-lawsuit) has secured its largest enterprise deployment to date through an expanded partnership with Deloitte that will make its [Claude AI](https://technologymagazine.com/news/how-claudes-sonnet-4-5-sets-a-new-ai-coding-standard) assistant available to more than 470,000 employees across 150 countries.

The deal, announced on Monday, builds on a collaboration the two companies first unveiled last year and represents a significant milestone for the AI start-up as it competes with rivals including OpenAI and Google for enterprise customers.

![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/AJpK3YTTKZ4/hqdefault.jpg)

## Financial commitment and deployment scale

The partnership involves substantial investment from both parties, though neither company disclosed specific financial details.

"We are both investing a significant amount in this partnership, whether that's financial or whether it is just simply the engineering resource that we're going to put into this as well," says Paul Smith, CCO at Anthropic.

Deloitte will develop different Claude "personas" tailored to specific employee groups, ranging from accountants to software developers, over the coming months.

The consulting firm is establishing a Claude Centre of Excellence staffed with specialists who will help teams deploy the technology more rapidly.

Paul Smith, CCO at Anthropic

## Training and certification programmes

As part of the collaboration, Deloitte and Anthropic are co-creating a formal certification programme to [train 15,000 professionals on Claude](https://technologymagazine.com/articles/why-reddit-sues-anthropic-the-dangers-of-ai-data-privacy).

These certified practitioners will support Claude implementations across Deloitte's network and assist with the firm's internal AI transformation efforts.

The deployment comes as Deloitte seeks to demonstrate its own AI capabilities to clients while helping them navigate their digital transformations.

"Our clients obviously want to know: 'Are you using it as well?' So we can advise them better, we can be more credible," explains Ranjit Bawa, Deloitte's Chief Strategy & Technology Officer for the US.

"That's why we said we got to start with ourselves as we continue to have our clients reimagine their future."

Ranjit Bawa, Deloitte's Chief Strategy & Technology Officer for the US

## Industry-specific solutions

The partnership will focus on developing AI solutions for regulated industries including financial services, healthcare, life sciences and public services.

These solutions will combine Claude's design approach with Deloitte's Trustworthy AI framework to provide transparency in model decision-making.

"Deloitte chose Claude because they need trusted AI that can help their employees and clients across industries and on a global scale – from coding and software development to customer engagement and industry-specific advisory," Paul says.

"When the world's leading organisations need to tackle complex, critical work, they choose Anthropic because Claude is built for the compliance and control that enterprises demand."

![Youtube Placeholder](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/Yct0MvNtdfU/hqdefault.jpg)

## Slack integration expands reach

The Deloitte announcement follows Anthropic's recent launch of a Slack integration that allows users to access Claude directly within their Slack workspaces.

The integration enables employees to work with Claude through direct messages, an AI assistant panel or by mentioning the assistant in thread conversations.

Users can also connect Slack to Claude's apps, allowing the AI to search and reference relevant Slack messages when providing responses.

The integration maintains existing Slack permissions, with Claude only accessing channels and conversations that users have permission to view.

"Every company is on its way to becoming an agentic enterprise, where AI agents work hand-in-hand with humans," explains Rob Seaman, Chief Product Officer of Slack at Salesforce.

"Partnering with Anthropic to integrate Claude into Slack and Slack context into Claude accelerates that journey – bringing best-in-class AI directly into the flow of work."

Rob Seaman, Chief Product Officer of Slack at Salesforce

## Broader enterprise momentum

The partnerships come as Anthropic works to expand its global presence and enterprise customer base.

The start-up has accumulated 300,000 business customers since its founding four years ago, with nearly 80% of usage coming from international markets.

In September, Anthropic announced plans to triple its international workforce this year and appointed Chris Ciauri as MD of International to lead the expansion.

The company also announced its latest model, Claude Sonnet 4.5, in late September alongside news that it had closed a US$13bn funding round at a US$183bn post-money valuation.

Chris Ciauri as MD of International at Anthropic

## Demonstrating AI value internally

The Deloitte deployment reflects a broader trend of enterprises seeking to demonstrate AI capabilities through internal adoption before advising clients.

By exposing its employees to Claude, Deloitte aims to generate productivity gains whilst inspiring staff to consider how the technology could transform other industries and sectors.

"Deloitte is making this significant investment in Anthropic's AI platform because our approach to responsible AI is very aligned, and together we can reshape how enterprises operate over the next decade," Ranjit says.

The firm noted that Claude continues to be a leading choice for many clients as well as its own AI transformation efforts.

Paul expresses that the company remains focused on execution despite the competitive landscape.

"We're still pretty busy," he says. "But it's good busy."

## Company portals

* ![](https://assets.bizclikmedia.net/127/2284a6205ceaddd6803d59645e364330:42d6314520592270c98e41d11b3ce36e/picture)
